DP Name: Sustainability Statement Objective
Mapped Frameworks: GRI, IFRS S1, IFRS S2, TCFD
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 1 (Foundation) sets a parallel objective of reporting impacts for stakeholders. IFRS S1 para. 1 and IFRS S2 para. 1 set the objective of informing investors on sustainability-related risks and opportunities. TCFD frames the same purpose from a financial risk lens. Core objective statement is shared across all four frameworks — differences are in audience emphasis.
De-duplication Notes: The sustainability statement objective narrative is a single canonical framing exercise. ESRS emphasises dual materiality (impact + financial). GRI emphasises impact on stakeholders. IFRS S1/S2 and TCFD emphasise investor-relevant financial materiality. Draft once for ESRS; adjust framing for other frameworks.
Schema / Unit: Narrative statement of purpose and scope of the sustainability statement
Tonality Requirement: Declarative and objective. State the purpose clearly. Avoid promotional language. Align with the dual perspective: impact on people/environment and financial effects on the undertaking.
Trigger Condition: Mandatory for all in-scope companies. The sustainability statement must communicate the undertaking's impacts on people and the environment, and information material to users on sustainability-related risks and opportunities.
Framework Schema Variants:
GRI: GRI 1 Foundation describes equivalent reporting objectives; no separate disclosure item — absorbed into the GRI index and basis of preparation
TCFD: Final recommendations introduction states equivalent objectives — framed around investor-useful information; omit impact materiality framing
IFRS S1: Para 1–3 states objectives — more investor/capital market focused than ESRS; omit double materiality framing; emphasise enterprise value relevance
IFRS S2: Para 1–2 climate-specific objectives — scope narrower than ESRS; restrict to climate-related matters only

DP Name: Four Reporting Areas
Mapped Frameworks: GRI, IFRS S1, IFRS S2, TCFD
Cross-Framework Bridge: TCFD is structured identically across the same four pillars (Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets). IFRS S1 para. 6 uses the same four-pillar structure. GRI topics map across all four areas. This structural alignment means a single four-pillar architecture can organise disclosures for ESRS, TCFD, and IFRS S1/S2 simultaneously.
De-duplication Notes: The four reporting areas are isomorphic with TCFD's four pillars and IFRS S1's structure. A single structural template covering all four areas, organised once, satisfies the structural requirement across all three frameworks. Only the specific content items within each pillar differ by framework.
Schema / Unit: Narrative description organised across four areas: governance, strategy, impacts/risks/opportunities management, metrics and targets
Tonality Requirement: Structural and organisational. This DP establishes the disclosure architecture. Responses under each of the four areas should follow the stated structure consistently throughout the sustainability statement.
Trigger Condition: Mandatory for all in-scope companies. Sustainability disclosures must be organised across the four reporting areas: (1) governance, (2) strategy, (3) management of material impacts/risks/opportunities, and (4) metrics and targets.
Framework Schema Variants:
GRI: GRI 3-3 covers management of material topics across same four reporting areas — less prescriptive about area structure; map to GRI topic management approach sections
TCFD: Four pillars (Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets) map closely to ESRS areas — use TCFD pillar labels when reformatting for TCFD output
IFRS S1: Four pillars identical to TCFD by design; use ISSB pillar labels
IFRS S2: Same four pillars as IFRS S1 applied to climate-specific content only; restrict scope accordingly

DP Name: Application: ESRS 1 with ESRS 2 and Topical Standards
Cross-Framework Bridge: No direct cross-framework equivalent. This is an ESRS-internal architectural rule. Other frameworks have analogous meta-documents (e.g. GRI 1: Foundation, IFRS S1 as overarching standard) but they operate differently.
De-duplication Notes: ESRS-only meta-requirement. Not a content disclosure point — governs the relationship between ESRS 1 and the topical standards. No data collection required; relevant for the basis of preparation note in the sustainability statement.
Schema / Unit: Narrative description of how ESRS 1 general requirements apply in conjunction with ESRS 2 and topical standards
Tonality Requirement: Procedural and architectural. This requirement describes the relationship between standards, not a disclosure in itself. If referenced in the sustainability statement, use concise, factual language to describe the reporting framework applied.
Trigger Condition: Mandatory. ESRS 1 applies together with ESRS 2 (general disclosures) and all applicable topical standards (E1–E5, S1–S4, G1). It does not generate standalone disclosure outputs but governs how all other ESRS disclosures are prepared.

DP Name: Entity-Specific Disclosures for Material Topics Not Covered by ESRS
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 3 (Material Topics) para. 14 similarly requires disclosure of material topics not covered by GRI topic Standards, using GRI 3 as the disclosure vehicle. Strong structural parallel — both frameworks require entity-specific disclosures for uncovered material topics.
De-duplication Notes: Entity-specific disclosures are by definition unique to the undertaking and topic. However, where a GRI entity-specific disclosure under GRI 3 covers the same material topic, the same underlying content can be reframed for ESRS para. 11. Collect once; reframe for each framework's structural requirements.
Schema / Unit: Entity-specific narrative or quantitative disclosures covering material sustainability matters not addressed by any ESRS topical standard
Tonality Requirement: The entity-specific disclosure must follow the same quality standards as prescribed ESRS disclosures — complete, neutral, accurate, comparable. Clearly label the disclosure as entity-specific. Describe the topic, the associated IROs, and the undertaking's response.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when the undertaking identifies a material sustainability topic or impact that is not covered by any ESRS topical standard (E1–E5, S1–S4, G1). The undertaking must develop and disclose entity-specific information for that topic.
Framework Schema Variants: GRI: No direct GRI equivalent for entity-specific disclosures; GRI 101 allows entity-specific standards when no GRI Topic Standard covers a topic — present as a supplement to the GRI index with a note on the topic gap being addressed

DP Name: Comparability in Entity-Specific Disclosures
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 2-4 (Restatements of information) and GRI 2-5 (External assurance) address comparability and restatements. IFRS S1 para. 55–57 addresses comparative information and restatements. All frameworks share the same comparability principle — disclose changes, restate where practicable, explain where not.
De-duplication Notes: Comparability is a quality requirement that applies across all frameworks. A single methodology note and restatement disclosure, drafted once, can satisfy ESRS para. 12, GRI 2-4, and IFRS S1 para. 55 simultaneously with minor framing adjustments.
Schema / Unit: Narrative or quantitative disclosure maintaining year-on-year comparability; consistent methodologies and metrics across reporting periods
Tonality Requirement: Process-oriented and transparent. When disclosing changes in methodology or metrics, explain the reason, the effect on comparability, and any restated prior-period figures. Do not change metrics year-on-year without explanation.
Trigger Condition: Applies whenever entity-specific disclosures are made under para. 11. Entity-specific disclosures must be prepared consistently across reporting periods to allow comparability. Changes in methodology or scope must be disclosed and explained.
Framework Schema Variants:
GRI: No direct comparability requirement — inferred from GRI 3-3 (management of material topics); restate as a consistency note within the management approach section
IFRS S1: Para 78 requires comparative period information — explicitly requires prior period figures where material; add prior-year column to any quantitative disclosures

DP Name: Fair Presentation: Complete, Neutral and Accurate
Schema / Unit: Narrative: statement of compliance with fair presentation principles
Tonality Requirement: Factual and objective. No selective emphasis. Both positive and adverse information must be presented with equal rigour.
Trigger Condition: Applies to the sustainability statement as a whole. Completeness, neutrality and accuracy are minimum quality thresholds for every disclosure.

DP Name: Fair Presentation: Comparable, Verifiable and Understandable
Schema / Unit: Narrative: methodology consistency, audit trail documentation, plain-language presentation
Tonality Requirement: Clear, accessible and methodologically consistent. Define technical terms. Maintain year-on-year consistency unless change is disclosed.
Trigger Condition: Applies to the sustainability statement as a whole. Comparability, verifiability and understandability are quality standards for every disclosure.

DP Name: Double Materiality: Impact and Financial Perspectives
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI: Impact materiality only (single materiality). TCFD/IFRS S2/ISSB: Financial materiality only. ESRS is unique in requiring both simultaneously. Double materiality is the primary structural differentiator between ESRS and all other major frameworks.
De-duplication Notes: No equivalent dual-lens requirement exists in GRI, TCFD, ISSB or BRSR. ESRS double materiality cannot be satisfied by financial materiality assessments alone. Separate impact assessment process required.
Schema / Unit: Narrative: dual-lens assessment covering impact materiality and financial materiality
Tonality Requirement: Analytical and structured. Describe both the impact and financial perspectives with equal weight. Do not subordinate one to the other.
Trigger Condition: Foundational requirement applying to the entire materiality assessment process. Both lenses must be applied to every ESRS topic.

DP Name: Materiality Filter: Include and Omit Based on Materiality
Schema / Unit: Narrative: documented materiality conclusions per topic and per DR
Tonality Requirement: Analytical. Materiality conclusions must be defensible under audit. Both inclusions and exclusions must be documented.
Trigger Condition: Applies to every disclosure point in every ESRS standard. Operates at both topic level and individual DR level within material topics.

DP Name: Two-Step Materiality Process: Topic Level then DR Level
Schema / Unit: Narrative: documented two-step materiality assessment conclusions
Tonality Requirement: Process-oriented and structured. Describe the two steps clearly. Must be auditable.
Trigger Condition: Mandatory process requirement. Step 1 = topic-level assessment. Step 2 = DR-level assessment within each material topic. Both steps must be documented.

DP Name: Disclosure Obligation: All Material DRs for Material Topics
Schema / Unit: Narrative: all DRs from material ESRS standards necessary for fair presentation
Tonality Requirement: Comprehensive and structured. Do not cherry-pick DRs within a material topic.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when any sustainability topic is assessed as material under Para 22/25. Requires disclosure of all information in the relevant standard necessary for fair presentation.

DP Name: Information Scope: Always-Disclose DRs (ESRS 2 + Minimum Topical)
Schema / Unit: Narrative: mandatory ESRS 2 disclosures + minimum topical DRs regardless of materiality
Tonality Requirement: Mandatory and unconditional. These disclosures cannot be omitted regardless of materiality assessment conclusions.
Trigger Condition: ESRS 2 in full + specific topical DRs marked as always-disclose must be reported irrespective of the materiality assessment outcome for any topic.

DP Name: Phase-in Relief: Deferred Obligations for Specific DRs
Phased-in Details: Phase-in applies per Appendix C of ESRS 1. Year 1 companies may omit certain DRs. Years 2–3 progressively add requirements. Always-disclose DRs (Para 29) are not eligible for phase-in.
Schema / Unit: Narrative: identification of applicable phase-in provisions and explanation of which DRs are deferred
Tonality Requirement: Transparent about what is being deferred and under which provision. Must not create impression that the information is not material.
Trigger Condition: Available to companies in their first 1–3 years of CSRD application. Specific DRs listed in Appendix C may be deferred. Company must disclose which reliefs are being used.

DP Name: Materiality Evidence Standard: Reasonable and Supportable Conclusions
Schema / Unit: Narrative: documented evidence basis for materiality conclusions
Tonality Requirement: Evidential and defensible. Each conclusion must reference specific facts, data or stakeholder input.
Trigger Condition: Applies to every materiality conclusion — both inclusions (material) and exclusions (not material). Evidence must be available and defensible.

DP Name: Annual Review of Materiality Assessment
Schema / Unit: Narrative: description of annual review process and any changes to materiality conclusions
Tonality Requirement: Process-oriented. Describe what changed, what was reviewed, and what conclusions were maintained or revised.
Trigger Condition: Required at least annually, coinciding with each reporting cycle. Must be triggered earlier if significant changes to business activities, stakeholder context or regulatory environment occur.

DP Name: Materiality Outcome: List of Material IROs
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 3-2 (List of material topics). TCFD Strategy a (climate-related risks and opportunities). IFRS S1 para. 18 (sustainability-related risks and opportunities). All frameworks require a disclosed output list, but scope differs: GRI is topic-level; TCFD/IFRS S2 is climate only; ESRS covers all E, S and G topics through dual lens.
De-duplication Notes: The ESRS IRO list is the broadest of all frameworks. GRI material topics are a subset. TCFD/IFRS climate R&O are a subset. One master ESRS IRO list can generate all required outputs with appropriate filtering and reframing.
Schema / Unit: Structured list of material impacts, risks and opportunities by topic, with supporting rationale
Tonality Requirement: Structured and specific. Name the actual IROs — do not describe process steps only. Each IRO should be identifiable to a topic and perspective (impact or financial or both).
Trigger Condition: Required output of the materiality assessment process. Must be disclosed as part of ESRS 2 IRO-1. Drives the full scope of the sustainability statement.

DP Name: Impact Materiality: Actual and Potential Impacts on People and Environment
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 3-3 (Management of material topics — impact identification). OECD Guidelines for MNEs (due diligence on impacts). UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (salient issues). Impact materiality is the closest analogue in ESRS to the GRI/UNGPs impact due diligence lens.
De-duplication Notes: GRI 3-3 covers impact identification for material topics. ESRS goes further by requiring systematic coverage of all ESRS topics through the IRO lens, not just self-selected material topics. GRI impact materiality and ESRS impact materiality are conceptually aligned but ESRS scope is broader.
Schema / Unit: Narrative: description of actual and potential impacts, positive and negative, own operations and value chain
Tonality Requirement: Descriptive and evidence-based. Name specific impacts. Distinguish actual from potential. Do not limit to own operations.
Trigger Condition: Required for the impact materiality perspective of the dual materiality assessment. Covers own operations and upstream/downstream value chain.

DP Name: Impact Materiality Criteria: Severity and Likelihood
Schema / Unit: Narrative: severity assessment (scale, scope, irremediability) + likelihood for potential impacts
Tonality Requirement: Analytical and criteria-based. Must reference the three severity dimensions explicitly. Likelihood must be assessed for potential (not yet occurring) impacts.
Trigger Condition: Defines the criteria for determining whether a negative impact is material under the impact perspective. Must be applied to all negative impacts identified in Para 39.

DP Name: Impact Materiality: Positive Impacts and Significance Criteria
Schema / Unit: Narrative: description of significant positive impacts on people and environment
Tonality Requirement: Balanced and credible. Positive impacts must be substantiated — do not include aspirational claims without evidence of actual or potential benefit.
Trigger Condition: Applies when positive impacts have been identified in the Para 39 assessment. Significance (not severity) is the materiality criterion for positive impacts.

DP Name: Financial Materiality: Risks and Opportunities from Sustainability Matters
Cross-Framework Bridge: TCFD Strategy a-b (climate-related risks and opportunities). IFRS S1 para. 9-12 (sustainability-related risks and opportunities). IFRS S2 (climate-specific risks and opportunities). Financial materiality in ESRS is conceptually equivalent to enterprise value materiality in TCFD/ISSB — the key difference is ESRS also includes access to finance and cost of capital as financial dimensions.
De-duplication Notes: TCFD/ISSB financial R&O and ESRS financial materiality assessment are largely equivalent in method and scope for climate. For non-climate topics (S1–S4, G1), ESRS financial materiality has no direct TCFD/ISSB equivalent. A TCFD/IFRS S2 financial risk/opportunity assessment can serve as the ESRS financial materiality assessment for E1, with supplementation for other topics.
Schema / Unit: Narrative: sustainability-related financial risks and opportunities affecting financial position, performance and cash flows
Tonality Requirement: Financially oriented. Connect sustainability matters to their financial effects. Use financial risk language. Reference time horizons.
Trigger Condition: Required for the financial materiality perspective of the dual materiality assessment. Covers risks and opportunities arising from sustainability matters that affect financial performance.

DP Name: Financial Materiality: Connections to Financial Statements
Schema / Unit: Narrative: description of how sustainability-related risks/opportunities connect to line items in the financial statements
Tonality Requirement: Financially specific. Reference balance sheet, P&L or cash flow line items where possible. Bridge sustainability language to financial reporting language.
Trigger Condition: Applies when financially material sustainability matters have been identified under Para 43. Requires explicit connection to financial statement line items.

DP Name: Financial Materiality Criteria: Likelihood and Magnitude
Schema / Unit: Narrative: likelihood and magnitude assessment for financial risks and opportunities
Tonality Requirement: Analytical. Both dimensions (likelihood and magnitude) must be addressed. Reference time horizons explicitly.
Trigger Condition: Criteria for determining whether a sustainability-related risk or opportunity is financially material. Applied as part of the financial materiality assessment under Para 43.

DP Name: Financial Materiality: Definition of Financial Effects
Schema / Unit: Narrative: classification of financial effects across financial position, performance, cash flows, access to finance and cost of capital
Tonality Requirement: Definitional and structured. Map identified risks/opportunities to the relevant financial effect dimension(s).
Trigger Condition: Definitional requirement for the financial materiality assessment. Establishes the five dimensions of financial effect that must be considered.

DP Name: Topics Can Be Material Under Both Perspectives Simultaneously
Schema / Unit: Narrative: identification of topics material under both impact and financial perspectives
Tonality Requirement: Clarifying and structured. Where a topic is material under both lenses, explicitly state so and describe the nature of each type of materiality separately.
Trigger Condition: Applies when a sustainability topic is assessed as material under both the impact and financial perspectives. The two perspectives are not mutually exclusive.

DP Name: Interdependencies: Impacts Generate Financial Risks and Opportunities
Schema / Unit: Narrative: description of how the company's impacts connect to and generate its sustainability-related financial risks and opportunities
Tonality Requirement: Causal and connected. Describe the mechanism by which an impact creates a financial risk or opportunity. Avoid treating the two perspectives as unrelated silos.
Trigger Condition: Applies where impacts identified under the impact perspective generate or could generate financial risks or opportunities. Requires explicit linkage in the disclosure.

DP Name: Basis for Preparation — General basis for sustainability statement
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 BP-1 (basis for preparation) can reuse TNFD General Requirements-style disclosures on scope, boundary, reporting period, and approach for nature-related reporting, including LEAP scoping decisions. Use TNFD scoping/boundary statements as the nature module within the broader ESRS BP-1 basis statement.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD has an explicit reporting boundary and scope narrative (entities, value chain, geographies, time horizon), reuse it for BP-1 and harmonise boundary definitions across ESRS and TNFD.
Schema / Unit: Narrative description of reporting scope, consolidation basis, reporting period, and methodology choices
Tonality Requirement: Technical and declarative. State scope and boundary clearly. Reference ESRS 1 general requirements where applicable. Describe any entity-specific approaches or departures from standard methods. Use neutral, audit-ready language.
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Often describes LEAP scope and reporting boundary; ESRS requires explicit sustainability statement basis, consolidation scope, and reporting period details.

DP Name: Basis for Preparation — Disclosures in relation to specific circumstances
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 BP-2 (specific circumstances / omissions / phase-ins) is supported by TNFD LEAP scoping guidance: define LEAP scope up front (geographies, business lines, value chain segments) acknowledging cost/time/data constraints; document stakeholder engagement and third‑party expert use; and treat LEAP as iterative/repeatable. Reuse these scoping decisions as the rationale/evidence for any ESRS basis exceptions, estimation limits, and phased-in disclosures, ensuring transparency about constraints and iteration plans.
De-duplication Notes: Use one consolidated ‘scope & constraints’ memo (LEAP scope + data limitations + iteration plan) to satisfy both TNFD transparency expectations and ESRS BP-2 explanations for exclusions, estimates, and phased-in application.
Schema / Unit: Narrative disclosure of specific circumstances affecting reporting (e.g. transitional provisions, non-availability of data, entity-specific metrics)
Tonality Requirement: Explanatory and exception-based. Clearly state what specific circumstance applies and how it affects disclosures. Be specific — vague statements ('data not yet available') are insufficient without timeline and remediation plan. Required where Column K override applies.
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory). Use whenever disclosures are affected by data availability constraints, estimation, or phased-in provisions.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Scope statement emphasises LEAP assessment boundary and iteration; ESRS: requires explicit disclosure of circumstances, estimation uncertainty, omissions, and phased-in usage, with clear justification and forward plan.

DP Name: Governance — Board oversight of sustainability matters
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 GOV-1 (board oversight) maps conceptually to TNFD Governance recommended disclosures (Governance A–C): board oversight, management role, and integration into governance structures for nature-related dependencies/impacts/risks/opportunities. Reuse TNFD governance mapping (committees, mandates, frequency, nature competence building) and reframe into ESRS governance disclosure style (roles, responsibilities, oversight mechanisms).
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD governance disclosures already drafted, reuse as the nature-specific subsection within ESRS 2 GOV-1, and ensure ESRS covers the broader sustainability perimeter (not only nature).
Schema / Unit: Narrative description of governance body composition, roles, and oversight mechanisms
Tonality Requirement: Formal institutional voice. Describe roles, responsibilities, and processes. Use present tense. Avoid vague language — cite specific committee names, meeting frequencies, and decision-making authority.
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Governance narrative may be nature-specific; ESRS requires consolidated sustainability governance narrative with clear board/AMSB accountability and reporting lines.

DP Name: Governance — Management role in sustainability reporting and oversight
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 GOV-2 (management role) can leverage TNFD’s governance expectations for assigning clear management responsibility for nature-related issues, resourcing LEAP teams, using third‑party expert advice where needed, and running LEAP as an iterative enterprise process. Reuse TNFD governance RACI (roles across risk, sustainability, operations, procurement, finance) as the nature component of GOV-2.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD LEAP team structure and decision cadence exist, reuse it for GOV-2: management accountability + cross-functional involvement + expert support; ensure it is embedded in overall sustainability governance.
Schema / Unit: Narrative describing management-level roles, reporting lines, and controls for sustainability
Tonality Requirement: Institutional and procedural. Describe roles and reporting lines clearly. Use named roles or titles rather than general descriptions. Distinguish between management oversight and board oversight.
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Management governance is nature-specific and LEAP-operational; ESRS: requires consolidated management governance for sustainability reporting with controls and escalation paths.

DP Name: Governance — Integration of sustainability-related performance in incentive schemes
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 GOV-3 (incentives) can incorporate TNFD-aligned performance management by tying executive/management incentives to completion quality of LEAP (coverage, iteration cadence, stakeholder engagement integrity) and to outcomes reflected in TNFD Metrics & Targets (nature-related KPIs, target progress). Use TNFD metrics catalogue as candidate incentive KPIs; ensure metric definitions, units, and assurance-readiness are clear.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse the same TNFD KPI dictionary (definitions, calculation standards, disaggregation rules) as the KPI specification for any sustainability-linked incentive metrics under GOV-3.
Schema / Unit: Narrative — description of whether and how sustainability-related performance metrics are included in executive and senior management remuneration schemes; type of metric, weighting, governance body responsible
Tonality Requirement: Factual and governance-precise. Name the incentive schemes (short-term, long-term). State specific sustainability KPIs used, their weighting in total remuneration, and the governance body that sets and monitors them. If no linkage exists, state this explicitly.
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: KPI set is nature-specific; ESRS: requires disclosure of how sustainability performance is embedded in incentive schemes (governance/process + KPI examples), potentially across broader ESG topics.

DP Name: Governance — Statement on due diligence
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 GOV-4 (due diligence statement) can leverage TNFD General Requirements and governance disclosures that reference due diligence processes for nature-related issues, including meaningful engagement with IPLCs and affected stakeholders. Reuse TNFD due diligence process descriptions (scope, integration with ERM, stakeholder engagement, escalation) and reframe as an ESRS due diligence statement covering sustainability matters (nature included).
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD due diligence narrative exists (especially around stakeholder engagement and LEAP governance), reuse for GOV-4 and broaden to the full ESRS sustainability perimeter.
Schema / Unit: Narrative — mapping of how due diligence process is integrated into the undertaking's overall risk management and governance; reference to UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and OECD Guidelines
Tonality Requirement: Procedural and standards-referencing. Map each step of the due diligence process (identify, prevent, mitigate, account for, communicate, remediate) to the undertaking's actual procedures. Reference UNGP and OECD Guidelines explicitly. Describe board and management roles in due diligence oversight.
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Due diligence content is often nature-specific and tied to LEAP; ESRS requires a consolidated due diligence statement and governance accountability.

DP Name: Impact, Risk and Opportunity Assessment — Process for identifying and assessing material IROs
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 IRO-1 (IRO process) is the ESRS-wide analogue of TNFD LEAP. Use LEAP as the backbone methodology for identifying and assessing nature-related IROs; then integrate with ESRS double materiality process (impact + financial) across all sustainability matters. Key reuse: LEAP scoping, interface inventory, dependency/impact assessment, prioritisation logic → ESRS IRO identification narrative and process controls.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD LEAP has been conducted, reuse process documentation (scope, governance, data sources, stakeholder engagement, prioritisation) for ESRS 2 IRO-1; extend beyond nature to other ESRS topics as needed, but keep LEAP as the nature module within the enterprise process.
Schema / Unit: Process description — methodology, scope, data sources, stakeholder engagement, frequency, and outputs of IRO identification and assessment
Tonality Requirement: Methodological and process-oriented. Describe the steps, criteria, and tools used. Reference any external standards or consultants used. Distinguish between impact materiality and financial materiality processes. Use active voice and specific verbs (e.g. 'the company assessed', 'the process involves').
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory). This is the core ‘how we did materiality/IRO assessment’ disclosure.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Method is LEAP with nature-specific tools; ESRS: requires explicit double materiality framing, coverage of all sustainability topics, and linkage to ESRS topical materiality outcomes.

DP Name: IRO Assessment — Disclosure requirements covered by the undertaking's sustainability statement
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 IRO-2 (disclosure requirements covered) is a coverage/index disclosure that can be supported by TNFD reporting architecture artifacts: mapping of TNFD recommended disclosures to report sections, and any internal crosswalk tables. Use the TNFD disclosure inventory and crosswalk to substantiate which disclosure requirements are addressed and where (including any ‘not applicable’).
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD already maintains a disclosure inventory (recommended disclosures × report sections), reuse it as the basis for IRO-2 coverage mapping; add ESRS-specific requirement references and explicit location pointers within the sustainability statement.
Schema / Unit: Index/table — complete list of all ESRS disclosure requirements addressed in the sustainability statement, with location references (paragraph/page) and explanation of omissions or phase-in applications
Tonality Requirement: Index-style and cross-referencing. Provide a table listing every applicable ESRS disclosure requirement, its location in the sustainability statement, and reasons for any omissions. This is the compliance index — it must be exhaustive and precisely cross-referenced. State phase-in decisions explicitly with applicable Appendix C citations.
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Coverage may be shown as a TNFD index; ESRS requires a structured list of ESRS DRs covered and where they appear, plus explanations for omissions.

DP Name: Strategy — Business model, value chain, and sustainability context
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 SBM-1 (business model & value chain) overlaps with TNFD General Requirements + Strategy disclosures that require describing how the organisation’s business model interacts with nature across the value chain and geographies. Reuse TNFD interface inventory and priority locations summary to describe where in the value chain the organisation depends on/impacts nature, and how this links to strategy and operating context.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD has produced an interface inventory and priority location map, reuse them as the nature evidence pack for SBM-1; add ESRS-specific framing (material sustainability matters, value chain description) and ensure consistent entity boundary definitions.
Phased-in Details: Column L identifies specific SBM-1 sub-elements subject to phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: Narrative with optional diagrams; describes business model elements, sectors, geographies, value chain structure
Tonality Requirement: Strategic and descriptive. Present the business model objectively. Include upstream/downstream value chain mapping. Must cover sectors, geographies, and key relationships. Avoid marketing language.
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Often structured around LEAP outputs; ESRS: requires SBM-1 structured narrative and linkage to IROs and strategy disclosures.

DP Name: Strategy — Interests and views of stakeholders
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 SBM-2 (interests and views of stakeholders) is directly supported by TNFD LEAP guidance on meaningful engagement, especially with Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities (IPLCs) and affected stakeholders during nature-related assessment. Reuse TNFD engagement logs, FPIC processes where applicable, and stakeholder input integration steps as evidence for SBM-2. Key delta: ESRS requires stakeholder views across all sustainability matters; TNFD provides the nature module with explicit IPLC emphasis.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD engagement work was done for LEAP (consultations, workshops, grievance inputs, third-party expert interviews), reuse the same stakeholder evidence pack for SBM-2; broaden to non-nature topics only as needed.
Phased-in Details: Column L: certain SBM-2 sub-elements subject to phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: Narrative — description of stakeholder engagement process, key stakeholder groups identified, their interests and views, and how these have been considered in strategy and materiality assessment
Tonality Requirement: Stakeholder-centric and process-oriented. Name key stakeholder groups. Describe engagement methods (surveys, dialogues, panels, grievance mechanisms). Explain how stakeholder input has influenced materiality assessment and strategic decisions. Reference double materiality connection. Avoid generic language — cite specific engagement activities.
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Engagement is embedded in LEAP and due diligence guidance; ESRS: requires structured disclosure of which stakeholders were engaged, how views were gathered, and how they influenced strategy and materiality outcomes.

DP Name: Strategy — Material impacts, risks and opportunities and their interaction with strategy
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS 2 SBM-3 (material IROs and strategy interaction) can leverage TNFD’s requirement to connect nature-related dependencies/impacts/risks/opportunities to business model, strategy, and financial planning (TNFD Strategy A–D). Reuse TNFD IRO register (from LEAP Assess) and map each nature-related IRO to strategy choices, affected parts of the business model/value chain, and decision implications (capex, product design, sourcing, risk appetite).
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD already has a structured IRO register plus resilience/scenario narrative, reuse it for SBM-3’s IRO inventory and strategy linkage; add ESRS-required structure (how IROs influence strategy and are influenced by strategy) and ensure the IRO set reconciles to the ESRS materiality outcome list.
Phased-in Details: Column L: certain SBM-3 sub-elements phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: Narrative + structured list of material IROs with time horizons, likelihood, and financial magnitude where applicable
Tonality Requirement: Strategic and risk-informed. Describe how material topics connect to and affect business strategy, financial position, and stakeholder outcomes. Use structured tables or lists for IRO catalogues. Include time horizons (short/medium/long-term). Forward-looking language is appropriate.
Trigger Condition: Always required (ESRS 2 mandatory).
Disaggregation Dimensions: By topic (climate / environment / social / governance) / by materiality type (impact / financial) / by IRO category (impact / risk / opportunity)
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Often structured as IRO register + strategy narrative; ESRS: requires explicit ‘interaction with strategy’ framing and linkage to sustainability statement structure and financial statement connections where relevant.

DP Name: Climate — Transition plan for climate change mitigation
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: TNFD does not introduce a separate climate transition plan requirement; however, TNFD encourages integrated climate–nature strategy. Use the existing ESRS/TCFD/IFRS S2 transition plan narrative and add nature-related integration where material (e.g., nature-based solutions, land-use change impacts, biodiversity safeguards).
De-duplication Notes: Treat ESRS E1-1 as the canonical transition plan. TNFD content is an integration overlay (nexus safeguards and nature-related dependencies for transition actions), not a separate plan.
Phased-in Details: Column L: Transition plan sub-elements subject to phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: Narrative description of the transition plan: decarbonization pathway, milestones, capital allocation, and alignment with 1.5°C or Paris Agreement goals
Tonality Requirement: Strategic and forward-looking. Describe the transition plan concretely — milestones, investment commitments, and technology pathways. Reference Paris Agreement alignment explicitly. Avoid vague net-zero commitments without underpinning data. Include locked-in assets and stranded asset risk if applicable.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Climate topic is material; ESRS transition plan expectations apply.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Add nature safeguard notes for transition actions (avoid maladaptation harming ecosystems). ESRS remains the base structure.

DP Name: Climate — Policies related to climate change mitigation and adaptation
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: Climate policies are primarily handled by ESRS/TCFD/ISSB. TNFD integration point is ensuring climate policies (mitigation/adaptation) consider nature impacts (e.g., biomass sourcing, offsets, NBS integrity, land/water constraints) and align with TNFD LEAP findings for priority locations.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse existing climate policy register for E1-2; add a ‘nature interaction’ review step (from TNFD LEAP) only where climate actions have material nature impacts.
Schema / Unit: Policy descriptions: scope, coverage, governance owner, date adopted, and how policies address climate mitigation and/or adaptation
Tonality Requirement: Policy language. Factual and declarative. Name specific policies. State their scope (which operations, geographies, value chain elements they cover). Indicate governance ownership and adoption date. If no policy exists, state this explicitly — omission is not sufficient.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Climate topic is material and policies exist; disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Adds nature-interaction checks; ESRS/TCFD remain primary disclosure formats.

DP Name: Climate — Actions and resources in relation to climate change policies
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: Climate actions (abatement, adaptation, transition investments) can be integrated with TNFD Prepare outputs where actions interact with nature (e.g., land-based mitigation, renewable siting impacts, water use for cooling/hydrogen). Use TNFD LEAP outputs to prioritise locations and to apply nature safeguards to climate action plans.
De-duplication Notes: Maintain one unified transition action register. Tag actions with ‘nature interaction’ where TNFD indicates material dependencies/impacts; avoid duplicating action registers for TNFD.
Schema / Unit: Narrative — description of climate-related actions taken and planned; resources allocated (CapEx, OpEx, €); timelines; governance owner; distinction between mitigation and adaptation actions
Tonality Requirement: Action-oriented and financially quantified. Describe specific actions taken under climate policies — not just intent. Quantify CapEx and OpEx allocated. Distinguish mitigation actions (reducing emissions) from adaptation actions (managing physical risk). Reference any recognised frameworks (SBTi, RE100, EV100). State milestones and progress to date.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Climate topic is material and actions exist (MDR-A gating).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Adds location prioritisation and nature safeguard fields; ESRS remains MDR-A structure for disclosure.

DP Name: Climate — Targets related to climate change mitigation and adaptation
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: Climate targets are ESRS/ISSB-native. TNFD integration point is ensuring climate targets and pathways account for nature constraints and co-benefits (e.g., land-use targets, NBS integrity, avoided biodiversity harm). Where NBS or offsets are used, link to TNFD metrics/targets discipline and disclose nature-related assumptions.
De-duplication Notes: Do not create TNFD climate target rows. Use ESRS E1-4 as canonical and add TNFD nexus notes only where targets depend on land/water/ecosystem outcomes.
Phased-in Details: Column L: certain target sub-elements phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: Targets: base year, target year, metric (tCO2e, %, absolute vs. intensity), scope covered, pathway reference (SBTi, Paris-aligned, etc.), and progress to date
Tonality Requirement: Precise and metrics-driven. State targets in quantitative terms wherever possible. Identify scope covered (Scope 1, 2, 3), whether target is absolute or intensity-based, and reference any external validation (e.g. SBTi approval). Pair with current-year progress metric.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Climate topic is material and targets exist; disclose absence where required.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By target type (GHG reduction / energy / adaptation) / by scope (Scope 1 / Scope 2 / Scope 3) / by time horizon (short / medium / long-term)
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Adds nature dependency/impact assumptions for targets relying on NBS/offsets. ESRS/ISSB remains base.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: tCO2e for GHG targets; % reduction relative to base year
TCFD: % reduction from base year; absolute or intensity; state whether SBTi-aligned
IFRS S2: tCO2e absolute or intensity ratio; clearly state base year and target year
GRI: tCO2e or %; GRI 305-5 (reduction of GHG emissions) used for quantitative target tracking
CDP: C4.1 format — specific % or absolute target; sector classification; base year; target year; % achieved to date

DP Name: Climate — Energy consumption and mix
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E1-5 (energy consumption and mix) is climate/energy reporting; TNFD only integrates where energy sourcing has material nature impacts (e.g., biomass, hydropower, land footprint). Use TNFD LEAP to flag and contextualise nature dependencies/impacts for energy sourcing decisions, but keep ESRS as the metric format source.
De-duplication Notes: Collect energy data once for ESRS/ISSB; add TNFD location/land/water impact context only for material energy sources with nature implications.
Schema / Unit: MWh or GJ — total energy consumption, split by: fossil fuels, nuclear, renewable (self-generated vs. purchased). Energy intensity ratio (GJ per unit of revenue or production).
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and methodological. Report in MWh or GJ consistently across years. State methodology for energy accounting (operational control, equity share, etc.). Disclose renewable energy certificates (RECs) separately from actual renewable procurement. Include energy intensity metric with denominator defined.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Climate topic is material.
Calculation Standard: ESRS E1 par. 37–43; IEA energy statistics; Eurostat energy balances for conversion factors
Disaggregation Dimensions: By energy type (fossil / renewable) / by source (fuel combustion / purchased electricity / purchased heat & steam & cooling) / by geography if material
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Adds nature-context narrative where relevant; no distinct TNFD metric format.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: MWh or GJ — total + fuel/electricity/heat split
GRI: MWh — GRI 302-1 (consumption within organisation) requires MWh with fuel type breakdown
CDP: GJ — CDP C8.2 uses GJ with renewable/non-renewable split and percent renewable
TCFD/IFRS S2: MWh or GJ as consistent with GHG reporting; typically absorbed into GHG intensity metric

DP Name: Climate — Gross Scopes 1, 2, 3 and total GHG emissions
Mapped Frameworks: CDP, ESRS, GRI, IFRS S2, Other
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: GHG emissions disclosures are climate-specific and generally not a TNFD-specific requirement. TNFD integration is limited to ensuring nature-related assumptions are transparent when emissions management relies on land-based mitigation, removals, or supply chain land-use change (biodiversity/deforestation). ESRS/GRI/ISSB/CDP remain the primary mapping for GHG accounting.
De-duplication Notes: No TNFD-specific GHG dataset needed. Reuse GHG Protocol dataset; only add TNFD nexus notes where land-use/nature intersects (e.g., FLAG emissions, deforestation).
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit Scope 3 and total GHG figures in Year 1 of sustainability reporting [Appendix C of ESRS 1, Column K]
Schema / Unit: tCO2e — Scope 1 (direct), Scope 2 (location-based and market-based), Scope 3 (all 15 categories), total GHG. GHG intensity per revenue or FTE.
Tonality Requirement: Highly quantitative and methodological. Report each scope separately in tCO2e. For Scope 2, report both location-based and market-based figures. For Scope 3, list all 15 categories — identify which are included and methodology for each. State GHG accounting standard used (GHG Protocol, ISO 14064). Disclose biogenic emissions separately.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Climate topic is material.
Calculation Standard: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004); GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance (2015); GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard (2011)
Disaggregation Dimensions: By GHG scope (Scope 1 / Scope 2 location-based / Scope 2 market-based / Scope 3 total + by category) / by GHG gas type (CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6, NF3) for Scope 1
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Adds nature nexus notes for land-based emissions/removals; core format unchanged.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: tCO2e — Scope 1 + Scope 2 (LB and MB) + Scope 3 total + by category; intensity ratios
GRI: tCO2e — GRI 305-1/2/3 each a separate disclosure; GRI 305-4 for intensity required separately
CDP: tCO2e — CDP C6 structured with Scope 1, Scope 2 (both methods), Scope 3 by category; biogenic CO2 separately
TCFD/IFRS S2: tCO2e — Scope 1 + 2 + 3 with narrative on Scope 3 categories included
BRSR: tCO2e — Scope 1 + Scope 2 total; intensity per INR crore of turnover

DP Name: Climate — GHG removals and carbon credits
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E1-7 (carbon credits/removals) is the main point where TNFD nature integrity becomes relevant: nature-based removals and offsets must avoid biodiversity harm, respect IPLC rights, and be transparent on location/ecosystem impacts. Use TNFD LEAP and engagement guidance to set integrity safeguards and disclosure notes for nature-based credits/removals.
De-duplication Notes: Use one carbon credit/removal inventory. Add TNFD safeguard checks (location/ecosystem impact, additionality, permanence, IPLC engagement) for nature-based credits; disclose deltas transparently.
Schema / Unit: tCO2e — volume of GHG removals (in-house and third-party), carbon credits purchased and retired, credit standard/registry, vintage year
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative with registry-level specificity. Separate removals from avoided emissions. State the standard for carbon credits (Gold Standard, VCS, etc.) and registry. Disclose vintage year. Do not conflate credits with direct emission reductions — these must be reported separately from gross emissions.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when credits/removals are used/disclosed.
Calculation Standard: GHG Protocol Land Sector and Removals Guidance; ISO 14064-2 for project-level removals
Disaggregation Dimensions: By removal type (biotic / geological / technological) / by carbon credit type (avoidance / removal) / by registry
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Adds biodiversity/IPLC integrity disclosures for nature-based credits; ESRS remains the reporting structure.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: tCO2e for removals; number of credits
GRI: No specific GRI standard for removals; disclosed as supplementary information under GRI 305-1 notes
CDP: tCO2e — CDP C11.4 (carbon credits); separate offset and removal distinction
TCFD: tCO2e; disclosed as part of net zero pathway narrative

DP Name: Climate — Internal carbon pricing
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: Internal carbon pricing is climate governance; TNFD integration is optional and primarily about ensuring internal pricing/decision tools also consider nature-related externalities where relevant (e.g., shadow prices for water/biodiversity in parallel). If the organisation runs a combined internal pricing framework, document alignment with TNFD metrics/targets for nature pricing inputs.
De-duplication Notes: Keep E1-8 canonical. Only reference TNFD if an integrated internal pricing framework exists (carbon + nature).
Schema / Unit: €/tCO2e — internal carbon price applied; type (shadow price, internal fee/levy, implicit); scope of application (investment decisions, product pricing, operational budgets); revenue from internal carbon levy if applicable
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and methodologically precise. State the carbon price level (€/tCO2e). Define the type of internal carbon pricing mechanism. Describe the scope of application — which decisions or business units it applies to. Reference alignment with external carbon price signals (EU ETS, SCC). If no ICP exists, state this and whether it is under consideration.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when internal carbon pricing exists.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By carbon pricing system (internal shadow price / external ETS / voluntary carbon market) / by scope of application (% Scope 1/2/3 covered)
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: May inspire parallel shadow pricing for nature; no distinct disclosure requirement.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: EUR/tCO2e (or reporting currency)
TCFD: USD/tCO2e typical; specify currency and whether shadow price or actual
CDP: CDP C11.3 — per tonne CO2e in reporting currency; structured fields for price type, coverage scope, and business strategy use
IFRS S2: Currency per tCO2e; note whether regulatory or voluntary

DP Name: Climate — Anticipated financial effects from material climate-related risks and opportunities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: Climate financial effects (E1-9) are largely covered by TCFD/ISSB. TNFD integration point is the climate–nature interaction: some financial effects arise from compounded climate+nature risks (e.g., water scarcity, ecosystem collapse affecting supply chains). Use TNFD LEAP outputs to enrich physical risk and dependency analysis where nature degradation is a key driver of operational and financial exposure.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse TCFD/ISSB climate financial analysis for E1-9; add TNFD-derived dependency/impact drivers only where they materially change physical risk assessment or resilience narrative.
Phased-in Details: Subject to phased-in provisions per Appendix C of ESRS 1 — quantitative financial effects may be deferred in early reporting years where methodology is not yet established
Schema / Unit: Quantitative (€ or % of revenue/assets at risk) + qualitative narrative; financial exposure to physical and transition risks over short/medium/long-term time horizons
Tonality Requirement: Financial and scenario-informed. Quantify financial exposure wherever possible. Distinguish physical from transition risk financial impacts. Reference scenario assumptions used (e.g. NGFS scenarios, IEA 1.5°C). Use ranges where uncertainty exists. Connect to balance sheet or income statement line items where feasible. Acknowledge limitations in quantification methodology.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Climate topic is material and financial effects are expected to be material.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By risk type (physical acute / physical chronic / transition policy / transition market / transition technology) / by time horizon (short / medium / long) / by financial effect type (revenue / cost / asset value / CapEx)
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Adds compounded-risk narrative; ESRS/TCFD remain core structure.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: EUR range or narrative where quantification not possible
TCFD: USD or reporting currency; scenario-referenced
IFRS S2: Reporting currency; linked to sensitivity analysis
CDP: CDP C2 format — estimated financial impact as a range in reporting currency

DP Name: Climate IRO Identification — Climate-related physical and transition risks and opportunities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: For climate, TNFD largely inherits the TCFD architecture rather than adding materially new climate disclosures. Where TNFD is used, climate risk/opportunity assessment should be integrated with nature-related IROs (e.g., land-use transition, nature-based solutions, supply chain physical risks). Reuse the organisation’s existing TCFD/ISSB climate risk process for ESRS E1 IRO-1, and ensure the ‘climate–nature nexus’ is captured where climate drivers affect ecosystems and where nature degradation amplifies climate physical risks.
De-duplication Notes: Do not create separate TNFD climate workstream: reuse TCFD/IFRS S2 climate IRO process as the canonical source; only add TNFD-specific integration notes (how climate scenario outputs interact with nature LEAP outputs).
Schema / Unit: Structured narrative: list of physical risks (acute/chronic), transition risks, and climate opportunities identified, with associated time horizons and assessment methodology
Tonality Requirement: Risk-analytical and forward-looking. Distinguish clearly between physical risks (acute vs. chronic) and transition risks (policy, technology, market, reputational). For each identified risk/opportunity, state: type, time horizon (short/medium/long), assessment methodology, and how it connects to financial impact. Use tables where multiple IROs are listed.
Trigger Condition: Always required for E1 IRO-1 sections (IRO-1 mandatory component in topic standards).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Climate disclosures are not primary; include a short nexus note where climate and nature risks interdepend. ESRS/TCFD/IFRS S2 remain the primary structure for climate IRO assessment.

DP Name: Pollution — Policies related to pollution prevention and control
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E2-1 (policies) can reuse TNFD governance/general requirement artifacts (policy inventory, boundary controls) plus pollution prevention policies arising from LEAP Evaluate/Assess (emissions controls, chemical management, spill prevention, supplier substance controls). Map into ESRS MDR-P structure for pollution.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse a single EHS/chemical management policy register for TNFD + ESRS E2-1; reformat into MDR-P fields (scope, commitments, implementation, monitoring) and include explicit gap disclosure when no policy exists for material pollution topics.
Schema / Unit: Policy descriptions covering scope, pollutants addressed, governance owner, regulatory alignment (IED, REACH, WFD)
Tonality Requirement: Policy language. Declarative and regulatory-aware. Name specific policies and the pollutants/media they address. Reference applicable EU regulatory requirements. State governance ownership and adoption date.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Pollution topic is material and policy exists (MDR-P gating); disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Pollution controls may be part of broader nature management; ESRS requires MDR-P formatted policy disclosure. CDP may require questionnaire-specific policy statements.

DP Name: Pollution — Actions and resources in relation to pollution prevention and control
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E2-2 (actions/resources) can be supported by TNFD Prepare-stage artifacts: pollution control action register (abatement, treatment, substitution, remediation), incident prevention controls, and effectiveness KPIs. Reuse TNFD action registers and monitoring to populate ESRS MDR-A action structure for pollution.
De-duplication Notes: Collect once: use one pollution abatement/remediation action register with CapEx/OpEx, timelines, and KPI tracking; tag for ESRS E2-2 and relevant CDP/GRI items; TNFD LEAP provides prioritised-location and impact materiality rationale.
Schema / Unit: Narrative — pollution abatement actions by medium (air, water, soil); CapEx/OpEx allocated (€); timelines; governance owner; distinction between preventive and remedial actions
Tonality Requirement: Action-oriented and financially quantified. Describe specific pollution abatement investments and process changes. Quantify CapEx and OpEx allocated. Reference applicable abatement technologies. Distinguish preventive (process design changes) from remedial (clean-up, compensation) actions. State milestones and progress.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Pollution topic is material and actions exist (MDR-A gating).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Actions may be captured per priority location; ESRS requires MDR-A formatting with explicit resources allocated and progress tracking.

DP Name: Pollution — Targets related to pollution prevention and control
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E2-3 (targets) aligns with TNFD Metrics & Targets: reuse target register artifacts (baseline, target year, progress) for pollution reduction (air emissions, water pollutants, soil contamination, hazardous substances). Ensure targets link to priority locations and material pollution pressures identified via LEAP.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse one pollution target register for ESRS E2-3; add ESRS-required disaggregation (by pollutant/medium/location) and comparative period expectations.
Schema / Unit: Pollution reduction targets — by medium (air/water/soil) and substance category; metric (% reduction, tonne reduction, concentration limit); base year; target year; regulatory compliance trajectory
Tonality Requirement: Precise and substance-specific. State targets by pollution medium and substance category. Reference regulatory compliance trajectories (EU Industrial Emissions Directive, Water Framework Directive) where applicable. Indicate whether targets are science-based, regulatory-minimum, or voluntary.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Pollution topic is material and targets exist; disclose absence/gap where required.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By pollutant type (air / water / soil) / by target metric (absolute / intensity) / by time horizon
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Targets may be location/pressure specific; ESRS requires MDR-T disclosure with baseline, milestones, and progress narrative; CDP may need additional formats.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Absolute or intensity; pollutant-specific units
GRI: No specific GRI target standard for pollution; reported as part of GRI 305-7 or 306-* management approach

DP Name: Pollution — Pollution of air, water and soil
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E2-4 (pollution of air, water, soil) can be grounded in TNFD dependency/impact assessment and metrics architecture: use LEAP Evaluate to identify relevant pollution pressures (emissions/discharges/releases) at priority locations, then report the ESRS-required quantitative disclosures. TNFD contributes the location/materiality logic; ESRS/GRI/CDP define the reporting formats.
De-duplication Notes: Collect once: a consolidated emissions/discharge/release dataset (by medium and pollutant class, with location tags) can satisfy ESRS E2-4 alongside corresponding GRI and CDP disclosures; TNFD LEAP provides prioritisation and boundary rationale.
Phased-in Details: Column L: certain sub-elements phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: Tonnes or kg — pollutant emissions to air (NOx, SOx, PM, VOCs, HAPs), discharges to water (N, P, heavy metals), and releases to soil; by substance and source
Tonality Requirement: Highly quantitative. Report by substance, emission medium, and source. Reference applicable regulatory emission limit values where relevant. State measurement methodology (direct measurement vs. calculation). Flag substances of concern separately. Include both operational and value chain sources where material.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Pollution topic is material; focus on significant pollution sources and regulated pollutants.
Calculation Standard: EU Industrial Emissions Directive (IED); E-PRTR Regulation; facility-level measurement per substance-specific EU limit values
Disaggregation Dimensions: By medium (air / water / soil) / by substance type (NOx, SOx, VOCs, PM, heavy metals, nitrogen/phosphorus) / by source
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Metrics should be linked to priority locations and nature impacts; ESRS requires structured pollution disclosures by medium; GRI/CDP may require additional breakdowns and questionnaire formats.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Metric tonnes or kg by substance
GRI: GRI 305-7 (NOx, SOx, and other significant air emissions) — report in metric tonnes; add breakdown by source type (combustion / process / fugitive)
CDP: CDP C12 — substances reported in metric tonnes with % change year-on-year

DP Name: Pollution — Substances of concern and substances of very high concern (SVHCs)
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E2-5 (substances of concern/SVHCs) can leverage TNFD LEAP Evaluate outputs to identify chemical/substance interfaces with nature (toxicity, persistence, bioaccumulation), priority locations/ecosystems exposed, and value chain substance flows. Use TNFD as the impact/materiality lens; then disclose ESRS-required substance inventories, phase-out plans, and controls.
De-duplication Notes: If a chemicals inventory and restricted substances list exists (REACH/SVHC), reuse it for E2-5; supplement with TNFD LEAP-derived prioritisation of substances/uses with highest nature impact (by location and exposure pathway).
Phased-in Details: Column L: phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: Tonnes — total mass of substances of concern and SVHCs generated, used, distributed, and released; by substance name and CAS number; lifecycle stage
Tonality Requirement: Chemically precise. Identify substances by name and CAS number. Distinguish substances of concern from SVHCs (REACH SVHC Candidate List). Report generation, use, distribution, and releases separately. Reference EU REACH regulation, POPs Convention, Minamata Convention lists.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Pollution topic is material and substances of concern are used/produced; requires inventory and management narrative.
Calculation Standard: REACH Regulation (EC) 1907/2006 for SVHC identification; EU Candidate List for SVHCs
Disaggregation Dimensions: By substance category (substance of concern / SVHC) / by medium (air / water / soil / product) / by site if material
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Focus on nature impact pathways and locations; ESRS requires SVHC inventory/management disclosures; CDP may require product-level chemical disclosures where applicable.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Metric tonnes / kg
GRI: GRI 301-1 (materials used) — by weight; GRI does not have a specific SVHC disclosure but materials use by type is reported

DP Name: Pollution — Anticipated financial effects from pollution-related impacts and dependencies
Mapped Frameworks: CDP, ESRS, IFRS S1, Other, TCFD
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E2-6 (anticipated financial effects) can leverage TNFD Strategy D and LEAP Assess/Prepare outputs linking pollution-related risks/opportunities to financial planning (capex for abatement/treatment, remediation liabilities, compliance costs, litigation risk, supply chain disruption, opportunity from cleaner products). Use TNFD risk/opportunity register and scenario analysis (where used), then reframe into ESRS financial effects structure with time horizons and line-item linkages where feasible.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD already produced quantified pollution liabilities/cost ranges and mitigation investment plans, reuse for E2-6; add ESRS-required time-horizon disaggregation and explicit link to E2 IROs and materiality outcomes.
Phased-in Details: Subject to phased-in provisions per Appendix C of ESRS 1 — quantitative financial effects may be deferred in early reporting years
Schema / Unit: € or % — quantitative financial exposure to pollution remediation costs, regulatory penalties, and transition costs; plus qualitative narrative where quantification not yet feasible
Tonality Requirement: Financial and risk-informed. Distinguish between current liabilities (ongoing remediation, fines) and anticipated future costs (regulatory tightening, transition investments). Reference specific regulatory drivers (IED review, REACH restrictions). Acknowledge methodology limitations where financial quantification is not yet established.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Pollution topic is material (and financial effects are expected to be material).
Disaggregation Dimensions: By impact/risk/opportunity type / by financial effect category (revenue / cost / asset impairment / liability)
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Pollution financial effects may be embedded in broader nature financial analysis; ESRS requires pollution-specific financial effects disclosure. IFRS S1/TCFD require enterprise-value framing; CDP may require questionnaire-specific financial impact tables.

DP Name: Pollution IRO Identification — Climate-related pollution impacts, risks and opportunities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E2 IRO-1 (pollution IRO identification) can leverage TNFD LEAP outputs to identify pollution-related dependencies/impacts/risks/opportunities (e.g., emissions to air/water/soil, hazardous substances, incidents, regulatory exposure) across priority locations and value chain. Use LEAP scoping + dependency/impact evaluation + prioritisation to structure the E2 IRO narrative. Key delta: frame explicitly as ESRS pollution IROs and connect to ESRS materiality outcome and MDR templates.
De-duplication Notes: If LEAP has produced a pressure/impact inventory and regulatory exposure assessment by location, reuse for E2 IRO-1; add ESRS-specific terminology and link to E2 DPs and MDR-P/A/T where relevant.
Schema / Unit: Structured narrative: pollutants identified, affected media (air/water/soil), associated risks and opportunities, assessment methodology
Tonality Requirement: Technical and risk-analytical. Identify specific pollutants and substances of concern. Reference relevant EU regulations (IED, REACH, CLP, Water Framework Directive). Distinguish between operational pollution and value chain pollution. State assessment methodology and data sources.
Trigger Condition: Always required for E2 IRO-1 sections (IRO-1 is mandatory component in topic standards).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Source artifacts include interface inventory, impact driver assessment, incident registers, regulatory mapping; render into ESRS pollution IRO narrative with value chain scope.

DP Name: Water & Marine — Policies related to water and marine resources
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E3-1 (policies) can reuse TNFD governance/general requirement artifacts (policy inventory, boundary/scoping controls) plus any water stewardship policies developed under LEAP (e.g. water use, discharge, marine impact prevention, supplier water expectations). Map the policy register into ESRS MDR-P structure for water and marine resources.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD policy register includes water stewardship policy elements, reuse it and reformat into ESRS MDR-P fields (scope, commitments, implementation, monitoring); supplement with CDP Water policy disclosures where available.
Schema / Unit: Policy descriptions covering water use, discharge quality, marine ecosystem protection, and catchment-level stewardship commitments
Tonality Requirement: Policy language with catchment-level specificity. Reference geographic scope of operations in water-stressed areas. Include commitments on water quality (discharge standards) and quantity (withdrawal limits). Reference external standards adopted (e.g. Alliance for Water Stewardship, CEO Water Mandate).
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Water & Marine topic is material and policy exists (MDR-P gating); disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Water policy may be in governance/policy register; ESRS requires MDR-P structure and explicit water/marine scope and gap disclosure if no policy exists.

DP Name: Water & Marine — Actions and resources related to water and marine resources
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E3-2 (actions/resources) can be supported by TNFD Prepare-stage artifacts: water action register (efficiency, reuse, discharge improvement), basin engagement plans, marine impact mitigation actions, supplier water programmes, and effectiveness KPIs. Reuse TNFD action registers and monitoring to populate ESRS MDR-A action structure for water and marine resources.
De-duplication Notes: Collect once: TNFD water action register + KPIs can be reused for ESRS E3-2; add ESRS-required disclosure of resources (CapEx/OpEx), timelines, and linkages to E3 targets and IROs.
Schema / Unit: Narrative — water efficiency, reuse, watershed protection, and marine conservation actions; CapEx/OpEx allocated (€); timelines; governance owner; focus on water-stressed areas
Tonality Requirement: Action-oriented. Describe specific water efficiency investments, reuse and recycling projects, and watershed/catchment engagement. Quantify CapEx/OpEx allocated. Reference AWS Alliance or CEO Water Mandate memberships where applicable. Distinguish site-level from catchment/landscape-level actions. Identify actions specific to water-stressed areas.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Water & Marine topic is material and actions exist (MDR-A gating).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Action registers may be LEAP Prepare outputs; ESRS requires MDR-A formatting with explicit resources allocated and progress tracking.

DP Name: Water & Marine — Targets related to water and marine resources
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E3-3 (targets) aligns with TNFD Metrics & Targets: reuse target register artifacts (baseline, target year, progress, restatements) for water withdrawal reduction, water efficiency, discharge quality, and basin-level targets. Map into ESRS MDR-T structure and ensure basin/materiality linkage is explicit.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD target register exists for water, reuse it for E3-3; add ESRS-required disaggregation (by water-stressed areas/basins) and comparative period expectations.
Schema / Unit: Water targets — metric (ML reduction, % intensity improvement, water-stressed area withdrawal reduction), base year, target year, SBTN freshwater target alignment
Tonality Requirement: Precise and metrics-driven. State targets quantitatively. Reference water-stressed area targets separately. Link to SBTN freshwater targets where used. Indicate site-specific vs. portfolio-wide scope. Report progress annually.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Water & Marine topic is material and targets exist; disclose absence/gap where required.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By target type (withdrawal / consumption / recycled / water-stressed areas) / by time horizon
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Targets may be tracked per location/basin; ESRS requires MDR-T disclosure with baseline, milestones, and progress narrative; CDP Water may require additional questionnaire-specific breakdowns.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Megalitres or m³
GRI: m³ — target tied to GRI 303-* disclosures
CDP: Megalitres or m³; CDP W9 format

DP Name: Water & Marine — Water consumption
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E3-4 (water consumption) is a core quantitative metric that can be grounded in TNFD dependency/impact assessment and metrics architecture. Reuse TNFD metrics catalogue for water (withdrawals, consumption, discharge) and ensure basin-level context (water stress) is captured. This DP is commonly cross-mapped to GRI 303 and CDP Water metrics; treat TNFD as the methodology layer that ensures the metric is decision-useful (location/basin, dependencies, impacts).
De-duplication Notes: Collect once: a single water accounting dataset (withdrawal/consumption/discharge) with basin and water-stress flags can satisfy ESRS E3-4, GRI 303 series, and CDP Water questions; TNFD LEAP provides the rationale for boundary and prioritised locations.
Phased-in Details: Column L: certain E3-4 sub-elements subject to phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: Megalitres (ML) — total water withdrawal by source (surface, groundwater, third-party), total water consumption, water in water-stressed areas (flagged separately), water intensity ratio
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and location-specific. Report total withdrawal and consumption separately (consumption = withdrawal minus discharge). Break down by source type. Flag volumes withdrawn in water-stressed areas using a recognised stress tool (WRI Aqueduct, WWAP). State water accounting methodology (operational control or equity share).
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Water & Marine topic is material; typically requires explicit focus on water-stressed areas and significant withdrawals/consumption.
Calculation Standard: GRI 303 Technical Protocol; WRI Aqueduct or WWF Water Risk Filter for water-stress classification
Disaggregation Dimensions: By source (surface / ground / seawater / third-party) / by water-stressed vs non-stressed areas / total consumption and recycled/reused
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Metrics should be linked to priority locations and dependency materiality; ESRS: requires specific water consumption disclosures (often with water-stressed area focus); GRI/CDP may require additional breakdowns and questionnaire formats.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Megalitres
GRI: m³ — GRI 303-3 (withdrawal), 303-4 (discharge), 303-5 (consumption); each separate disclosure
CDP: Megalitres — CDP W8.1 total withdrawal; add percentage change from prior year
BRSR: KL (kilolitres) — BRSR Principle 6; intensity = KL per INR crore turnover

DP Name: Water & Marine — Anticipated financial effects from water and marine resource dependencies
Mapped Frameworks: CDP, ESRS, IFRS S1, Other, TCFD
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E3-5 (anticipated financial effects) can leverage TNFD Strategy D and LEAP Assess/Prepare outputs linking water dependencies and water-related risks/opportunities to financial planning (capex for water efficiency/treatment, opex for water procurement, revenue at risk from water scarcity, compliance costs, supply chain disruption). Use TNFD risk/opportunity register and scenario analysis (where used) as the core dataset, then reframe into ESRS financial effects structure with time horizons and line-item linkages where feasible.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD already produced water risk quantification (ranges) and mitigation investment plans, reuse for E3-5; add ESRS-required disaggregation by time horizon and explicit link to material IROs from E3 IRO-1.
Phased-in Details: Subject to phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1 — financial quantification may be deferred in early years
Schema / Unit: € or % — financial exposure to water scarcity risks, regulatory costs, stranded asset risk in water-stressed locations; plus qualitative where quantification not feasible
Tonality Requirement: Financial and geographically grounded. Quantify financial exposure for operations in high or extremely high water-stress areas. Link to asset value at risk or operational cost exposure. Reference scenario tools (IPCC, NGFS physical risk scenarios). Acknowledge limitations.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Water & Marine topic is material (and financial effects are expected to be material).
Disaggregation Dimensions: By risk type (physical / regulatory / market) / by time horizon / by financial effect type
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Water financial effects may be embedded in broader nature financial effects; ESRS requires water/marine-specific financial effects disclosure. IFRS S1/TCFD require enterprise-value framing; CDP Water may require questionnaire-specific financial impact tables.

DP Name: Water & Marine IRO Identification — Water and marine resource impacts, risks and opportunities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E3 IRO-1 (water & marine IRO identification) can be materially supported by TNFD LEAP outputs. Reuse LEAP scoping (sites, basins, value chain water dependencies), dependency/impact evaluation (withdrawal, discharge, water stress exposure, marine impacts), stakeholder engagement (communities/water users), and prioritisation logic to produce the ESRS E3 IRO narrative. Key delta: express results explicitly in ESRS IRO framing (impacts/risks/opportunities) and connect to ESRS materiality outcomes for water and marine resources.
