De-duplication Notes: If LEAP already produced basin-level dependency/impact screening and a water risk register, reuse as E3 IRO evidence pack; only add ESRS-specific structure and terminology and link to ESRS MDR templates.
Schema / Unit: Structured narrative: water stress exposure, water-related risks, marine ecosystem dependencies, and opportunities, with assessment methodology
Tonality Requirement: Risk-analytical and watershed-aware. Identify water stress by geographic location (using AQUEDUCT or WRI tools). Distinguish between water withdrawal risks, water quality risks, and marine ecosystem dependencies. Reference relevant EU regulatory frameworks (Water Framework Directive, Marine Strategy Framework Directive).
Trigger Condition: Always required for E3 IRO-1 sections (IRO-1 is mandatory component in topic standards).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Source artifacts include basin/location screening, dependency/impact assessment, water risk/opportunity register; render into ESRS IRO narrative with basin-level specificity and value chain coverage.

DP Name: Biodiversity — Transition plan and consideration of biodiversity in strategy and business model
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E4-1 is strongly supported by TNFD Strategy recommended disclosures (Strategy A–D) plus the TNFD requirement to link strategy to priority locations and nature-related dependencies/impacts/risks/opportunities. Reuse TNFD Strategy narrative (business model + financial planning + resilience + transition/response plan) and adapt into ESRS E4-1 structure (including MDR-P/MDR-A/MDR-T linkages where applicable).
De-duplication Notes: Collect once: TNFD Strategy disclosures and supporting registers (priority locations, interface linkage, scenario outputs, transition/response plan register) can be reused to draft E4-1; add ESRS-specific MDR structure and ESRS phrasing.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for undertakings ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — biodiversity transition plan; no-net-loss/net-positive commitment; integration of biodiversity into business model and capital allocation; Kunming-Montreal GBF alignment; milestones and 2030 targets
Tonality Requirement: Strategic and science-informed. Reference Kunming-Montreal GBF (especially Target 15 on business disclosure). Reference SBTN nature targets where adopted. Describe integration of biodiversity into capital allocation and product/service design. This is the nature equivalent of ESRS E1-1 (climate transition plan).
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Biodiversity topic is material (ESRS topical disclosure), but relies on IRO-1 results; phased-in exemptions may apply for ≤750 employees.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Use TNFD STR-A/B/C/D narrative as source; ensure ESRS E4-1 explicitly references ESRS-required policy/action/target hooks and ESRS materiality outcomes.

DP Name: Biodiversity — Policies related to biodiversity and ecosystems
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E4-2 (policies) can draw from TNFD Governance and General Requirements artifacts (policy inventory, human rights/IPLC engagement policies, sensitive location handling, evidence/approval controls) plus any TNFD-aligned biodiversity/nature policies. Map TNFD policy inventory + implementation governance into ESRS MDR-P structure for biodiversity.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD policy register exists, reuse it as the policy source-of-truth and only reformat into ESRS MDR-P fields (scope, commitments, implementation, monitoring).
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit all E4 DPs except IRO-1 for first 2 years. If E4 is material, must still disclose ESRS 2 par. 17-BP2 [Column K]
Schema / Unit: Policy descriptions covering biodiversity protection, no net loss/net positive commitments, land use, and ecosystem service stewardship
Tonality Requirement: Policy language with site-level and landscape-level awareness. Reference the mitigation hierarchy (avoid, minimize, restore, offset). Note any no-net-loss or nature-positive commitments. Reference relevant international frameworks (Kunming-Montreal GBF, EU Biodiversity Strategy). Include supply chain biodiversity policies where applicable.
Trigger Condition: Disclose if Biodiversity topic is material and relevant policies exist (ESRS MDR-P gating); still document ‘no policy’ explicitly where applicable.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Policies may be organised as governance/policy registers; render into ESRS MDR-P template sections (policy scope, commitments, implementation, monitoring).

DP Name: Biodiversity — Actions and resources related to biodiversity and ecosystems
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E4-3 (actions/resources) is supported by TNFD Prepare-stage artifacts: nature action register, transition/response plan register, mitigation hierarchy approach, control effectiveness KPIs, and remediation logs. Reuse TNFD action register and effectiveness monitoring to populate ESRS MDR-A action structure and E4-3 narrative/metrics.
De-duplication Notes: Collect once: use TNFD action register + effectiveness KPIs; reframe actions into ESRS action categories and explicitly state resources, timelines, and tracking per ESRS MDR-A fields.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for undertakings ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — habitat protection, restoration, and species conservation actions; CapEx/OpEx allocated (€); timelines; no-net-loss/net-gain implementation approach; governance owner
Tonality Requirement: Action-oriented and ecologically specific. Describe habitat protection, restoration, and species conservation actions. Quantify CapEx/OpEx allocated. Reference TNFD LEAP action outcomes. Distinguish on-site (in/adjacent to sensitive areas) from landscape-level or offsetting actions.
Trigger Condition: Disclose when Biodiversity topic is material and actions exist (ESRS MDR-A gating); otherwise disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Action registers (avoid/reduce/restore/offset/engage) map directly; add ESRS-required ‘resources allocated’ and MDR-A formatting.

DP Name: Biodiversity — Targets related to biodiversity and ecosystems
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E4-4 (targets) aligns with TNFD Metrics & Targets disclosures and target register artifacts (baselines, horizons, progress, restatements). Use TNFD targets register + performance tables and adapt to ESRS MDR-T structure and ESRS E4 target requirements.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD targets register exists, reuse it and add ESRS-specific fields (material IRO linkage, required disaggregation, comparative period) per MDR-T.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit for first 2 years (except ESRS 2 par. 17-BP2 if material) [Appendix C of ESRS 1]
Schema / Unit: Targets: type (no net loss, net positive, species recovery, habitat restoration), baseline year, target year, metric (ha, species count, biodiversity index), alignment with SBTN/Kunming-Montreal GBF
Tonality Requirement: Precise and science-based. Reference SBTN (Science Based Targets for Nature) or equivalent methodology where available. Targets should be location-specific where feasible. Distinguish between targets for operations and value chain. State baseline and reference any external validation.
Trigger Condition: Disclose if Biodiversity topic is material and targets exist; otherwise disclose absence/plan per ESRS rules.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By target type (land / freshwater / marine) / by target category (no net loss / net positive / area protection) / by time horizon
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Target tracking may be in target register + performance tables; render into ESRS MDR-T sections and ensure ESRS-required link to IROs and biodiversity impacts/dependencies.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Hectares; or qualitative target statement
GRI: Hectares — GRI 304-4 (IUCN Red List species and national conservation list species)

DP Name: Biodiversity — Impact metrics related to biodiversity and ecosystems
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E4-5 (impact metrics) is strongly supported by TNFD Metrics & Targets architecture: impact driver metrics, state of nature/ecosystem services metrics (where used), KPI dictionary, disaggregation rules, baseline/time series, and assurance-ready evidence bindings. Reuse TNFD metrics catalog + KPI dictionary + disaggregation specs and map into ESRS E4-5 required metric set; capture any ESRS-only additions (habitat change, species metrics, ecosystem service change) as deltas in the Sub-Metric Inventory.
De-duplication Notes: Use TNFD canonical metric register + unit conversion rules as the single source of truth; generate ESRS E4-5 tables as one rendering of those canonical metrics with ESRS-specific disaggregation and required comparatives.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit for first 2 years [Appendix C of ESRS 1]
Schema / Unit: Hectares — land use (total footprint, converted, degraded, restored), species affected (threatened species on site), ecosystem condition indicators, mean species abundance (MSA) where applicable
Tonality Requirement: Ecological and spatially explicit. Report land use metrics by type (agricultural, built-up, natural, semi-natural). Identify threatened species on-site by IUCN Red List category. Report changes from baseline year. Reference any biodiversity measurement methodology used (PREDICTS, GLOBIO, TNFD metrics). Be explicit about scope (direct operations vs. value chain).
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Biodiversity topic is material; comparative periods often expected for metrics and should be aligned with TNFD baseline/trend artifacts.
Calculation Standard: Mitigation hierarchy (avoid / reduce / restore / offset); IPBES biodiversity metrics; GRI 304 Technical Protocol
Disaggregation Dimensions: By impact type (land use / freshwater use / climate change / pollution / invasive species / exploitation) / by site / by ecosystem type
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Prefer using TNFD core/global indicators + driver metrics as backbone; add ESRS-specific metric elements and formatting (MDR links; ESRS-specific disaggregation).
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Hectares; number of species
GRI: Hectares; species count by IUCN Red List category — GRI 304-1, 304-2, 304-4

DP Name: Biodiversity — Anticipated financial effects from material biodiversity and ecosystem-related risks and opportunities
Mapped Frameworks: ESRS, IFRS S1, IFRS S2, Other, TCFD
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E4-6 (anticipated financial effects) can leverage TNFD Strategy D and Metrics & Targets pillars where organisations link nature-related risks/opportunities to financial planning and disclose anticipated financial impacts. Reuse TNFD risk/opportunity register, scenario analysis outputs (where used), and financial planning linkages (CapEx/OpEx, revenue at risk/opportunity, impairments/provisions) and render them in ESRS-required financial effects framing (short/medium/long term, value chain where relevant).
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD already produced a nature-related risk/opportunity register with quantified financial impacts (or ranges) plus scenario narratives, reuse as the core dataset for E4-6; add ESRS-specific disaggregation by time horizon and explicit reconciliation to material IROs from E4-IRO-1.
Phased-in Details: Subject to phased-in provisions per Appendix C of ESRS 1; Years 1–2 for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: € or % revenue/assets at risk — financial exposure to ecosystem service loss, land-use regulation changes, nature-related physical risks, transition risks from nature policy and markets
Tonality Requirement: Financial and scenario-informed. Distinguish physical (ecosystem service loss) from transition (regulation, carbon/nature markets) financial effects. Reference TNFD or IPBES ecosystem services valuation methodology. Use ranges where uncertainty exists. Acknowledge that nature-related financial quantification methodology is still maturing.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Biodiversity topic is material (and when financial effects are expected to be material); relies on IRO-1 outputs and the organisation’s financial planning processes.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By risk/opportunity type / by time horizon / by financial effect category
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Financial effects may be described as nature-related financial risk/opportunity and resilience narrative; render into ESRS structure with explicit time horizons, financial statement line-item linkages where possible, and materiality justification.

DP Name: Biodiversity IRO Identification — Biodiversity and ecosystem impacts, risks and opportunities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: This ESRS E4 IRO identification DP is substantially supported by TNFD LEAP (Locate–Evaluate–Assess–Prepare) outputs, especially interface inventory, priority locations, dependency/impact evaluation, and materiality/prioritisation logic. Use TNFD LEAP artifacts as primary evidence inputs, then express them in ESRS IRO framing (impacts/risks/opportunities) with ESRS-required granularity and terminology. Key reuse: interface inventory + priority locations + dependency/impact assessment results → ESRS IRO list and narrative basis. Key delta: ESRS expects explicit ESRS materiality framing and linkage to ESRS MDR templates where topic is material.
De-duplication Notes: If company already executed TNFD LEAP, do not re-run separate ESRS E4 discovery: map LEAP outputs into ESRS E4 IRO structure; only add ESRS-specific fields (materiality lens wording, ESRS-required stakeholder view articulation).
Schema / Unit: Structured narrative: sites in/near sensitive areas, biodiversity impacts (land use, species, invasive species), dependencies on ecosystem services, risks and opportunities, assessment methodology
Tonality Requirement: Ecological and site-specific. Reference location of operations relative to Natura 2000, Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs), and IUCN Red List habitats. Identify both direct impacts (land use change, pollution, overexploitation) and indirect impacts (supply chain). Reference TNFD or SBTN methodology if used. Include ecosystem service dependencies.
Trigger Condition: Always required for ESRS E4 (IRO-1 section), regardless of topic materiality outcomes; forms basis for E4 materiality and downstream E4 disclosures.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Source artifacts are LEAP outputs (interface inventory, priority locations, dependency/impact assessments, issue register). Render as ESRS IRO narrative + required ESRS tables/structure (if any).

DP Name: Resource Use — Policies related to resource use and circular economy
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E5-1 (policies) can reuse TNFD governance/general requirement artifacts (policy inventory, boundary controls) plus any circular economy/resource stewardship policies arising from LEAP (sustainable sourcing, recycled content, waste prevention, product design for circularity). Map into ESRS MDR-P structure for resource use and circular economy.
De-duplication Notes: If a TNFD-aligned resource stewardship policy register exists, reuse it for E5-1 and reformat into MDR-P fields (scope, commitments, implementation, monitoring), including gap disclosure when no policy exists for a material E5 topic.
Schema / Unit: Policy descriptions for circular economy, waste prevention, material efficiency; governance owner, scope, EU Circular Economy Action Plan alignment
Tonality Requirement: Policy language. Cover material efficiency, waste prevention hierarchy (reduce, reuse, recycle), and circular design principles. Reference EU Circular Economy Action Plan or equivalent. Distinguish operational policies from product/service design policies.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Resource Use & Circular Economy topic is material and policy exists (MDR-P gating); disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Policy may be framed as resource/nature stewardship; ESRS requires MDR-P structure and explicit circularity scope (materials, packaging, waste).

DP Name: Resource Use — Actions and resources related to resource use and circular economy
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E5-2 (actions/resources) can be supported by TNFD Prepare-stage artifacts: circularity action register (design changes, material substitution, recycling/reuse systems), supplier programmes, and effectiveness KPIs. Use LEAP priority locations and value chain hotspots to prioritise actions; report in ESRS MDR-A format including CapEx/OpEx and timelines.
De-duplication Notes: Maintain one circularity action register; TNFD LEAP provides hotspot rationale and location/value chain focus, ESRS requires MDR-A formatting and resource allocation disclosure.
Schema / Unit: Narrative — circular economy and waste reduction actions; CapEx/OpEx allocated (€); product redesign initiatives, take-back schemes, waste diversion programmes, critical raw material substitution actions; timelines
Tonality Requirement: Action-oriented. Describe specific circular economy investments. Quantify CapEx/OpEx. Reference EU Circular Economy Action Plan alignment. Distinguish actions reducing resource inflows (material efficiency, virgin material substitution) from those managing resource outflows (waste diversion, recycling).
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Resource Use & Circular Economy topic is material and actions exist (MDR-A gating).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Actions may be prioritised by nature impact hotspots; ESRS requires MDR-A structure with explicit resources and progress tracking.

DP Name: Resource Use — Targets related to resource use and circular economy
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E5-3 (targets) aligns with TNFD Metrics & Targets discipline: reuse target register artifacts (baseline, target year, progress) for circularity and resource efficiency targets (recycled content, waste reduction, packaging reduction, material intensity). Link targets to LEAP-identified resource dependencies and impacts at priority locations/value chain segments.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD target register covers resource use/circularity, reuse it for E5-3 and add ESRS-required disaggregation and comparative expectations.
Schema / Unit: Resource use and waste targets — metric (% recycled content, % waste diverted, tonne waste reduction, material intensity), base year, target year, circular economy target framework alignment
Tonality Requirement: Precise and metrics-driven. State targets by resource inflow (recycled content %) and outflow (waste reduction, diversion rate). Reference EU Circular Economy Action Plan packaging recycling targets where applicable. Link to EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility) compliance targets.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Resource Use & Circular Economy topic is material and targets exist; disclose absence/gap where required.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By target type (material input reduction / recycled content / waste reduction / water use) / by time horizon
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Targets may be framed as nature-pressure reductions; ESRS requires MDR-T disclosure with baseline, milestones, and progress narrative.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Absolute tonnes or % targets
GRI: % of recycled material or tonnes

DP Name: Resource Use — Resource inflows (materials, water, and energy use)
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E5-4 (resource inflows) can be grounded in TNFD LEAP Evaluate by linking material inputs to nature-related dependencies/impacts (land, water, biodiversity pressures) and to priority locations in the value chain. Use TNFD to justify boundary, hotspot focus, and choice of material categories; report ESRS-required quantitative inflow metrics and circularity parameters.
De-duplication Notes: Collect once: a material input dataset (by material type, virgin vs recycled content, supplier geography) can satisfy ESRS E5-4 and relevant GRI materials disclosures; TNFD LEAP provides hotspot and nature-impact rationale.
Phased-in Details: Column L: certain E5-4 sub-elements subject to phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: Tonnes or m³ — total material inflows by type (renewable/non-renewable, recycled/virgin), weight of products and packaging, critical raw materials used
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and material-flow oriented. Report total material input by weight. Distinguish virgin vs. secondary (recycled/reused) material. Flag critical raw materials separately (EU CRM list). Include packaging materials. State methodology (mass balance, spend-based, or hybrid). Reference any product-level material passports where available.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Resource Use & Circular Economy topic is material.
Calculation Standard: EU Critical Raw Materials Act definitions; EN 15804 for product-level material flows where applicable
Disaggregation Dimensions: By material type (renewable / non-renewable) / by input category (raw materials / semi-manufactured goods / manufacturing ancillaries / products) / by criticality
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Emphasises nature impact hotspots and priority locations; ESRS requires structured quantitative inflow reporting. CDP may require product/packaging-specific splits.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Metric tonnes
GRI: Metric tonnes or kg — GRI 301-1 (materials used by weight)

DP Name: Resource Use — Resource outflows (waste and end-of-life)
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E5-5 (resource outflows) can use TNFD LEAP Evaluate/Assess outputs to prioritise waste streams and end-of-life pathways that create material nature impacts (leakage to ecosystems, hazardous waste, marine litter). TNFD adds impact pathway and priority-location logic; ESRS requires quantitative reporting of waste generation, diversion, disposal, and circularity outcomes.
De-duplication Notes: Collect once: a waste/outflow dataset (by waste type, hazardous/non-hazardous, treatment route, geography) can satisfy ESRS E5-5 and GRI 306 series; TNFD LEAP helps prioritise material streams and contextualise impacts.
Phased-in Details: Column L: certain E5-5 sub-elements subject to phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: Tonnes — total waste generated by type (hazardous/non-hazardous), by disposal route (reuse, recycling, recovery, landfill, incineration), products/components designed for end-of-life recovery
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and waste-classification accurate. Follow EU waste classification codes (EWC codes). Report hazardous and non-hazardous separately. Distinguish recycling from other recovery routes — do not aggregate. Include both operational waste and product end-of-life where applicable. State diversion rate and methodology.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Resource Use & Circular Economy topic is material.
Calculation Standard: EU Waste Framework Directive categories; Eurostat waste statistics methodology
Disaggregation Dimensions: By waste category (hazardous / non-hazardous) / by disposal method (recycling / composting / incineration with/without energy recovery / landfill / other) / by site if material
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Focus on leakage risk and ecosystem impacts; ESRS/GRI require structured waste reporting; CDP may require additional packaging and end-of-life details.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Metric tonnes
GRI: Metric tonnes — GRI 306-3 (waste generated), 306-4 (waste diverted), 306-5 (waste to disposal)
CDP: Metric tonnes — CDP C12 waste disclosure

DP Name: Resource Use — Anticipated financial effects from material resource use and circular economy risks and opportunities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E5-6 (financial effects) can leverage TNFD Strategy D and LEAP Assess/Prepare outputs connecting resource dependencies and circularity risks/opportunities to financial planning (commodity price volatility, supply disruption, regulatory EPR costs, CapEx for circular redesign, circular revenue opportunities). Use TNFD risk/opportunity register and scenario analysis (where used), then reframe into ESRS financial effects structure with time horizons and line-item linkage where feasible.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD already produced quantified resource dependency risk ranges and circular investment plans, reuse for E5-6; add ESRS-required time-horizon disaggregation and explicit link to E5 IROs/materiality outcomes.
Phased-in Details: Subject to phased-in provisions per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: € or % revenue/assets — financial exposure to raw material price volatility, resource scarcity, waste regulation tightening, critical raw material supply disruption; circular economy transition opportunities
Tonality Requirement: Financial and scenario-informed. Distinguish physical (resource scarcity, supply disruption) from regulatory (EPR levies, waste tax, packaging tax) financial effects. Quantify critical raw material cost exposure where applicable. Include circular economy transition opportunities as positive financial effects.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Resource Use & Circular Economy topic is material (and financial effects are expected to be material).
Disaggregation Dimensions: By risk/opportunity type / by time horizon / by financial effect type
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Resource financial effects may be embedded in broader nature financial analysis; ESRS requires resource/circularity-specific financial effects disclosure; IFRS S1/TCFD require enterprise-value framing.

DP Name: Resource Use IRO Identification — Resource use and circular economy impacts, risks and opportunities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS E5 IRO-1 (resource use & circular economy IRO identification) can leverage TNFD LEAP outputs to identify material resource dependencies/impacts/risks/opportunities across priority locations and value chain (e.g., raw material sourcing pressures, land-use impacts, waste leakage, circularity opportunities). Use LEAP scoping + dependency/impact evaluation + prioritisation logic to structure the E5 IRO narrative; express explicitly in ESRS IRO framing and connect to ESRS materiality outcomes and MDR templates.
De-duplication Notes: If LEAP produced a material flow / input-output mapping and a dependency/impact register for resource use, reuse it as the evidence pack for E5 IRO-1; add ESRS-specific structure and terminology.
Schema / Unit: Structured narrative: material dependencies, resource scarcity risks, waste-related risks, circular economy opportunities, assessment methodology
Tonality Requirement: Resource-analytical and circularity-focused. Identify key material inputs and their scarcity risk (critical raw materials, virgin materials). Distinguish between resource-related risks (supply disruption, price volatility) and opportunities (circular business models, resource efficiency gains). Reference EU Critical Raw Materials Act and Circular Economy Action Plan where relevant.
Trigger Condition: Always required for E5 IRO-1 sections (IRO-1 mandatory component in topic standards).
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Source artifacts include interface inventory, material flow analysis (MFA) where available, sourcing footprint assessments, waste leakage risk registers; render into ESRS IRO narrative with value chain scope.

DP Name: Entity-specific — Cybersecurity / data breach incidents (if material)
Cross-Framework Bridge: Cyber/privacy is typically reported as an entity-specific sustainability matter if material. Can feed IFRS S1 risk and resilience disclosures and BRSR customer/privacy narratives (as applicable).
Schema / Unit: count — incidents/breaches; days — time to resolve; narrative — controls and response
Standard Reference: Entity-specific datapoint (not in baseline ESRS topical standards)
Trigger Condition: Use when cyber/privacy is identified as a material IRO and disclosed as entity-specific metric(s).
Framework Schema Variants:
IFRS S1: Link incidents to financial effects, risk management, and resilience narrative; may require quantitative sensitivity if material
BRSR: Often expects narrative plus counts of incidents/complaints in prescribed sections
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: count, days; severity categories
IFRS S1: may require financial effect estimates where material

DP Name: Business Conduct — Policies and corporate culture related to business conduct
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS G1-1 (business conduct policies and culture) can incorporate TNFD governance expectations by explicitly embedding nature-related conduct risks into the code of conduct and corporate culture (e.g., zero tolerance for illegal deforestation, wildlife trafficking, bribery in permitting of land/water use). TNFD does not replace G1-1; it supplies the nature-related risk content to be included in conduct policies and training.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD LEAP identified high-risk nature interfaces (land use, protected areas, permitting), reuse those findings to define ‘nature-sensitive’ conduct commitments in the code of conduct; avoid creating a separate TNFD conduct policy.
Schema / Unit: Policy descriptions covering anti-corruption, anti-bribery, anti-competitive behaviour, corporate culture, and whistleblowing mechanism
Tonality Requirement: Policy language aligned with international anti-corruption standards (UNCAC, OECD Anti-Bribery Convention). Reference specific policies (code of conduct, anti-bribery policy, gifts and hospitality policy, whistleblowing policy). State scope, training coverage, and governance owner. Reference any third-party certification (ISO 37001 Anti-Bribery Management System) where applicable.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Business Conduct topic is material; typically applicable for most undertakings.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Adds nature-risk conduct clauses; ESRS requires standard business conduct policy disclosure and governance ownership.

DP Name: Business Conduct — Management of relationships with suppliers and business partners
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS G1-2 (supplier and business partner relationships) can incorporate TNFD LEAP outputs to identify nature-related supply chain hotspots and integrate them into supplier due diligence (e.g., deforestation, water stress, biodiversity-sensitive sourcing). Use TNFD priority locations and interface inventory to strengthen supplier risk screening criteria and monitoring, and disclose the approach in ESRS business conduct terms.
De-duplication Notes: Use TNFD hotspot/priority location outputs as a procurement segmentation layer (which suppliers/sites need enhanced diligence). Keep one supplier diligence system; do not create TNFD-only questionnaires.
Schema / Unit: Narrative — supplier code of conduct requirements; ESG screening criteria in procurement; due diligence processes for business partners; exclusion/blacklisting procedures; CS3D alignment
Tonality Requirement: Process-oriented and governance-precise. Describe supplier code of conduct minimum standards and audit rights. Explain ESG screening criteria in procurement decisions. Reference EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CS3D) alignment. Describe blacklisting and contract termination procedures for non-compliant suppliers or business partners.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Business Conduct topic is material; supplier governance typically always relevant.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Supplier screening is framed as nature dependency/impact management; ESRS requires business conduct framing (due diligence, monitoring, relationship management).

DP Name: Business Conduct — Prevention and detection of corruption and bribery
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS G1-3 (prevention/detection of corruption and bribery) intersects with TNFD where nature-related permitting, land acquisition, water abstraction rights, and protected-area operations create elevated corruption risk. Use TNFD priority locations/interface inventory to prioritise corruption risk assessments and controls in nature-sensitive jurisdictions and disclose how controls are applied.
De-duplication Notes: TNFD does not add new data requirements. Use TNFD LEAP priority locations and permitting/land-use interface mapping to define which jurisdictions/activities are ‘nature-sensitive’ and therefore require enhanced anti-corruption controls and monitoring.
Schema / Unit: Narrative of anti-corruption/anti-bribery risk assessment process, due diligence procedures, internal controls, training coverage (%), and detection mechanisms
Tonality Requirement: Procedural and controls-oriented. Describe the risk assessment process for corruption and bribery. Reference specific internal control procedures. Report training coverage as a percentage of relevant employees. Describe detection mechanisms (hotline, audit, review processes). Reference any third-party due diligence on business partners.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Business Conduct topic is material; typically applicable where corruption risks exist.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Provides nature-sensitive hotspot focus; ESRS requires anti-corruption policy/control disclosure and monitoring.

DP Name: Business Conduct — Confirmed incidents of corruption or bribery
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS G1-4 (confirmed incidents of corruption/bribery) is not TNFD-native, but TNFD can inform risk segmentation: incidents associated with nature-related permitting, land-use approvals, resource access, or protected-area operations should be tagged and analysed as ‘nature-sensitive’ conduct risks for governance learning and prevention. Disclose incident counts per ESRS; use TNFD only to strengthen root-cause analysis and control improvements.
De-duplication Notes: No TNFD-specific dataset required. Extend the incident register taxonomy to include a ‘nature-sensitive interface’ tag derived from TNFD interface inventory (optional) to improve governance learning.
Schema / Unit: Number — confirmed corruption/bribery incidents in the reporting year; type of incident; actions taken; cases referred to law enforcement; contracts terminated due to corruption violations
Tonality Requirement: Factual and incident-specific. Report the number of confirmed incidents. State the nature of incidents at a category level (bribery, facilitation payments, fraud, conflict of interest). Describe corrective actions taken. Report referrals to law enforcement. Use neutral, legally careful language — avoid language that prejudges legal proceedings. If zero incidents, state explicitly (do not omit).
Trigger Condition: Triggered when incidents exist and Business Conduct topic is material.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By incident type (corruption / bribery) / by region / by outcome (dismissed / warned / legal action / settled)
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Adds optional tagging for nature-sensitive corruption vectors; ESRS/GRI remain the disclosure format.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Number of incidents
GRI: Number — GRI 205-3 requires incident count by nature (confirmed bribery / legal proceedings) and outcome

DP Name: Business Conduct — Political influence and lobbying activities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS G1-5 (political influence/lobbying) can incorporate TNFD where the undertaking engages on nature-related policy (biodiversity, land use, water regulation, nature markets). Use TNFD priority issues (from LEAP Assess/Prepare) to structure transparent disclosure of nature-related lobbying positions, trade association memberships, and alignment/misalignment risks.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD has a policy engagement register (issues, positions, memberships), reuse it as the nature module for G1-5 disclosures; avoid parallel registers.
Schema / Unit: Narrative + € amount — description of lobbying activities, political donations (amount and recipient type), trade association memberships with material policy positions, and governance of political engagement
Tonality Requirement: Transparent and disclosure-forward. Describe the nature and scope of lobbying activities. Report political donation amounts (even if zero — state explicitly). List trade associations where membership dues are used for lobbying. Reference the EU Transparency Register entry if applicable. Avoid vague statements — be specific about policy areas engaged on.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when the undertaking has political influence activities.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By type (political contributions / lobbying expenditure / trade association memberships / position by topic) / by country
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Adds nature-policy issue taxonomy; ESRS/GRI require lobbying disclosure format and governance controls.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: EUR for financial amounts
GRI: Reporting currency — GRI 415-1 (political contributions)

DP Name: Business Conduct — Payment practices
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS G1-6 (payment practices) has no direct TNFD equivalent. TNFD integration is indirect: where nature-related supply chains involve smallholders/IPLC-linked sourcing, fair payment practices and prompt payment can be described as enabling responsible nature stewardship and reducing social pressure that can drive unsustainable practices. Keep ESRS as the primary disclosure structure.
De-duplication Notes: Do not create TNFD-specific payment practice data. Where relevant, reference nature-linked supplier segments in the narrative as context only.
Schema / Unit: Days — average payment period for trade payables; % of invoices paid within agreed terms; % paid beyond 30/60/90 days; description of any late payment disputes
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and supplier-relationship aware. Report average payment period in days (separately for SME suppliers where feasible). State % of invoices paid within contractual terms. Reference compliance with EU Late Payment Directive. Flag any structural late payment practices and remediation. Be precise — this is a metric disclosure, not a narrative one.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when payment practices are relevant for disclosure.
Calculation Standard: EU Late Payment Directive (2011/7/EU); Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) calculation
Disaggregation Dimensions: By payment category (overdue 30–60 days / 60–90 days / >90 days) / by size of counterparty (SME vs non-SME)
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Context-only; ESRS remains primary format.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Days; %
GRI: % and amounts — no specific GRI payment practices disclosure

DP Name: MDR-A — Actions and resources adopted to manage material sustainability matters
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 3-3 (Management of material topics — actions element). TCFD Risk Management pillar (actions to manage climate risks). IFRS S1 para. 21 (actions taken and planned). MDR-A satisfies the 'actions' component of GRI 3-3 for each material topic. A unified action log per topic, tagged to the relevant ESRS standard and GRI 3-3 section, serves all frameworks.
De-duplication Notes: MDR-A is the universal actions template — reused across E1 through G1. GRI 3-3 actions element is functionally equivalent. One actions register per topic, tagged to GRI 3-3 and the relevant ESRS topical standard's action disclosure number (e.g. E1-3, S1-4), eliminates duplication.
Schema / Unit: Action description template — action name, objective, scope, timeline, resources allocated (€ capex/opex), progress to date, governance owner. Applied per material topic where actions have been taken.
Tonality Requirement: Action-oriented and evidence-based. For each material topic: describe specific actions taken (not just planned). Quantify resources allocated where possible (CapEx, OpEx). State timelines and milestones. Distinguish preventive from remedial actions. Avoid vague language — cite specific programmes, initiatives, or investments.
Trigger Condition: Triggered for each sustainability matter assessed as material where actions have been taken. MDR-A is a cross-cutting template applied within: E1-3, E2-2, E3-2, E4-3, E5-2, S1-4, S2-4, S3-4, S4-4. Per ESRS 1 par. 33, if no actions exist for a material topic, state this explicitly.
Framework Schema Variants:
GRI: GRI 3-3d (actions taken, including resources allocated) for each material topic — brief action description per topic; integrate into each topic's management approach section
TCFD: Risk Management pillar actions — describe risk mitigation and adaptation actions for climate topics; frame around risk category and time horizon
IFRS S1: Para 25 (actions taken) — describe specific actions and their intended outcomes; no MDR template structure

DP Name: MDR-P — Policies adopted to manage material sustainability matters
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 3-3 (Management of material topics — policy element). GRI 2-23 (Policy commitments). TCFD Strategy pillar (risk management policies). IFRS S1 para. 21 (sustainability-related policies). MDR-P satisfies the 'policy' element of GRI 3-3 management approach for each material topic. A single policy register with framework tags can serve all four simultaneously.
De-duplication Notes: MDR-P is the universal policy template in ESRS — reused identically across E1 through G1. GRI 3-3 policy element is functionally equivalent. One policy register per topic, tagged to GRI 3-3 and the relevant ESRS topical standard, eliminates duplication.
Schema / Unit: Policy description template — name, scope, governance owner, alignment to standards/frameworks, coverage of value chain, date adopted/updated. Applied to each material topic with a policy.
Tonality Requirement: Policy language. Factual and declarative. For each material topic: name the policy, state its scope (operations, value chain tiers), identify the governance owner, and reference relevant international standards (ILO, UNGP, ISO). If no policy exists for a material topic, state this explicitly and indicate intent or timeline.
Trigger Condition: Triggered for each sustainability matter assessed as material where a policy exists. MDR-P is a cross-cutting template applied within: E1-2, E2-1, E3-1, E4-2, E5-1, S1-1, S2-1, S3-1, S4-1, G1-1. Per ESRS 1 par. 33, if no policy exists, the undertaking must state this.
Framework Schema Variants:
GRI: GRI 2-23 (policy commitments) + GRI 3-3c (management approach — policy element) — GRI requires board-level approval statement; add board approval statement for each policy
TCFD: Governance pillar — describe policies governing climate risk assessment and management
IFRS S1: Para 24 — describe policies adopted; investor focus; include scope and governance accountability

DP Name: MDR-T — Targets set to manage material sustainability matters and measure progress
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 3-3 (Management of material topics — targets element). TCFD Metrics & Targets pillar (targets used to manage climate risks). IFRS S1 para. 21 (targets to manage sustainability risks and opportunities). MDR-T satisfies the 'targets' component of GRI 3-3 for each material topic. A unified targets register, tagged per framework and topical standard, eliminates duplication.
De-duplication Notes: MDR-T is the universal targets template — reused across E1 through G1. GRI 3-3 targets element is functionally equivalent. One targets register per topic, tagged to GRI 3-3 and the relevant ESRS topical standard (e.g. E1-4, S1-5), satisfies all frameworks.
Schema / Unit: Target description template — target name, metric, base year, target year, current performance, % progress, governance owner, whether science-based, link to executive remuneration. Applied per material topic where targets have been set.
Tonality Requirement: Precise and metrics-driven. For each material topic: state the target in quantitative terms (metric, base year, target year, current year value). Indicate whether the target is science-based or externally validated. State whether it is linked to executive remuneration. If no target exists, state this and indicate intent. Report progress against the target annually.
Trigger Condition: Triggered for each sustainability matter assessed as material where targets have been set. MDR-T is a cross-cutting template applied within: E1-4, E2-3, E3-3, E4-4, E5-3, S1-5, S2-5, S3-5, S4-5. Per ESRS 1 par. 33, if no targets exist, state this explicitly.
Disaggregation Dimensions: By topic / by target type (absolute / intensity / qualitative) / by time horizon
Framework Schema Variants:
GRI: GRI 3-3e (targets and performance against targets) — tabular format with target, baseline, current performance, and assessment of progress
TCFD: Metrics & Targets pillar — present climate-specific targets in tabular form with metric type, base year, target year, current value, % progress
IFRS S1: Para 26 — state each target, its metric, base year, target year, and whether validated/science-based

DP Name: Own Workforce — Policies related to own workforce
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S1-1 (own workforce policies) is not TNFD-native. TNFD contributes only indirectly where nature strategy and LEAP implementation affects workforce policies (skills, H&S for field operations, engagement for land/water management activities). Use TNFD governance/change-management artifacts to show how nature-related roles and responsibilities are embedded, but rely on ESRS/HR policy frameworks as the primary source.
De-duplication Notes: No TNFD-specific workforce policy dataset required. Maintain a standard HR policy register for S1-1; reference TNFD only when nature-related operational roles introduce additional policy needs (field safety, stakeholder engagement training).
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit all S1 DPs for Year 1 [Appendix C of ESRS 1, Column K]
Schema / Unit: Policy descriptions covering labour rights, working conditions, health and safety, equal treatment, freedom of association, and whistleblowing
Tonality Requirement: Policy language grounded in international labour standards. Reference ILO Core Conventions, UN Guiding Principles, and applicable EU Directives (Working Time, Equal Treatment, H&S). Name specific policies (code of conduct, H&S policy, DEI policy). State scope, governance ownership, and adoption date. Include whistleblowing/speak-up mechanism reference.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Own Workforce topic is material and policies exist; disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Internal governance for nature programs; ESRS requires MDR-P policy disclosure for workforce topics.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Processes for engaging with own workforce and workers' representatives
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S1-2 (engagement with own workforce) is not TNFD-native, but TNFD LEAP’s emphasis on cross-functional analyst teams and iterative assessment implies strong internal engagement, training, and consultation processes. Where nature-related strategy affects workforce (site operations, land/water management, transition plans), reuse TNFD internal governance and change-management artifacts (training plans, roles, internal workshops) as partial evidence for S1-2.
De-duplication Notes: No TNFD-specific workforce engagement dataset required. Reuse standard HR engagement mechanisms; reference TNFD only where internal LEAP governance created specific workforce training/engagement programs.
Phased-in Details: Year 1 exemption for undertakings ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — formal and informal workforce engagement channels; collective bargaining structures; frequency and methods; how workforce feedback is incorporated into management and board-level decision-making
Tonality Requirement: Process-oriented and stakeholder-inclusive. Describe formal engagement channels (trade unions, works councils, employee surveys, town halls) and informal channels. State % of workforce covered by formal engagement mechanisms. Explain how workforce views are escalated to management and board. Reference ILO standards on freedom of association where applicable.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Own Workforce topic is material.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: internal team/iteration emphasis; ESRS requires formal workforce engagement disclosure.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Processes to remediate negative impacts and channels for raising concerns
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S1-3 (remediation/channels) is not TNFD-native. TNFD’s UNGP-aligned engagement guidance can be reused at the process level: embed consistent grievance mechanism design principles (accessibility, non-retaliation, escalation, remedy) across all stakeholder groups, including employees. Use TNFD due diligence discipline to strengthen documentation quality; ESRS requires workforce-specific channels and outcomes.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse one UNGP-aligned grievance mechanism framework across workforce + IPLCs/communities; TNFD provides structure, ESRS S1-3 requires workforce-specific channel disclosure.
Phased-in Details: Year 1 exemption for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — grievance mechanism design per UNGP effectiveness criteria; remediation processes for work-related harms; speak-up/ethics hotline usage statistics where disclosed; number of grievances received, investigated, resolved
Tonality Requirement: Process-oriented and rights-aligned. Describe grievance mechanism design per UNGP effectiveness criteria (legitimate, accessible, predictable, equitable, transparent, rights-compatible). Reference non-retaliation protections explicitly. State number of grievances received, investigated, and resolved where disclosed.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Own Workforce topic is material and impacts exist.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: due diligence discipline; ESRS requires explicit worker grievance/remedy disclosure.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Taking action on material negative impacts and managing workforce-related risks
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S1-4 (actions) can intersect with TNFD where workforce actions are required to deliver nature-related risk management (e.g., training for site biodiversity/water management, resourcing LEAP teams, field protocols). TNFD provides internal capability-building rationale; ESRS requires workforce impact remediation and risk management actions.
De-duplication Notes: Do not create TNFD-specific workforce action registers. Where relevant, tag nature-programme capacity-building actions in the existing workforce action register and reuse across ESRS and TNFD governance narratives.
Phased-in Details: Year 1 exemption for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — workforce programmes and investments (H&S, training, equal pay, wellbeing, inclusion); CapEx/OpEx allocated; timelines; governance owner; distinction between preventive and remedial actions
Tonality Requirement: Action-oriented and evidence-based. Describe specific workforce programmes and investments. Quantify resources allocated. Distinguish preventive actions (training, policy enforcement) from remedial actions (incident response, compensation). Reference any external workforce standards adopted (ILO conventions, living wage certification, ISO 45001).
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Own Workforce topic is material and actions exist.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: capability-building actions for LEAP; ESRS requires S1-4 workforce impact management action disclosure.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Targets related to managing material negative impacts on own workers
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S1-5 (targets) is not TNFD-native. TNFD only contributes where internal capability targets are set to deliver nature-related governance (e.g., % relevant staff trained on LEAP, % sites with biodiversity/water competent teams). Use TNFD governance discipline for defining these internal targets, but ESRS remains the disclosure frame.
De-duplication Notes: No TNFD-specific dataset required. Use the standard HR target register; include nature-programme training/capability targets only if they are material to workforce impacts or governance commitments.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit S1 DPs including S1-5 in Year 1 [Appendix C of ESRS 1]
Schema / Unit: Targets: type (H&S, pay gap reduction, diversity, turnover), base year, target year, metric (TRIR rate, % pay gap, % representation), progress to date
Tonality Requirement: Precise and commitment-oriented. State targets in quantitative terms. Reference any science-based or externally validated targets (e.g. WEPs targets, IWBI WELL certification targets). Pair with current-year performance metric. Distinguish targets for operations vs. value chain. Note if targets are linked to executive remuneration.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Own Workforce topic is material and targets exist; disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: internal capability targets may be tracked; ESRS requires workforce impact target disclosure with baseline and progress.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Characteristics of the undertaking's employees
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 2-7 (Employees — headcount by gender, employment type, contract type, region). GRI 401-1 (New employee hires and employee turnover). BRSR Principle 3 (employee details). GRI 2-7 is the direct crossmap — structurally near-identical to S1-6. Companies with GRI 2-7 reporting satisfy S1-6 core metrics. BRSR also requires similar workforce demographics.
De-duplication Notes: GRI 2-7 is the canonical source. S1-6 and GRI 2-7 collect the same data with minor structural differences. Ensure gender disaggregation covers all three categories (male/female/other) to satisfy ESRS — GRI 2-7 often only requires male/female.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit S1-6 in Year 1 [Column L, Appendix C of ESRS 1]
Schema / Unit: Headcount — total employees, by gender (male/female/other), by contract type (permanent/temporary), by employment type (full-time/part-time), by region/country, employee turnover rate
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and HR-data accurate. Report as of reporting date (headcount, not FTE). Break down by gender, contract type, and employment type at minimum. Geographic breakdown by region is required. State headcount methodology and any consolidation boundary differences from financial reporting.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when own workforce is assessed as material. Disclose employee headcount characteristics. Phased-in for ≤750 employees in Year 1.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Characteristics of non-employee workers in the undertaking's own workforce
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 2-8 (Workers who are not employees — total number, breakdown by type, working location). GRI 2-8 is near-identical to S1-7 in definition and structure. Collect once to GRI 2-8 standard; reformat for ESRS.
De-duplication Notes: GRI 2-8 and ESRS S1-7 are functionally equivalent for non-employee worker headcount. Single data collection satisfies both.
Phased-in Details: Year 1 exemption for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Headcount or FTE — total non-employee workers (contractors, agency workers, freelancers) by type; primary working location; methodology and data limitations acknowledged
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative with data limitation transparency. Report number of non-employee workers. Distinguish contract types (self-employed, agency workers, other). State primary work location. Acknowledge data limitations — non-employee headcount is often held by agencies and may require estimation. State methodology used.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when own workforce is material. Phased-in for ≤750 employees Year 1.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Collective bargaining coverage and social dialogue
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 2-30 (Collective bargaining agreements — % of employees covered, by region). GRI 403-4 (Worker participation and consultation — H&S committee coverage). GRI 2-30 collective bargaining coverage % directly satisfies the core metric in S1-8.
De-duplication Notes: GRI 2-30 and ESRS S1-8 are functionally equivalent for collective bargaining coverage. GRI 2-30 data directly satisfies S1-8 core metric. GRI 403-4 adds the H&S committee coverage dimension.
Phased-in Details: Year 1 exemption for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: % of total employees covered by collective bargaining agreements; by country/region; type of representation (trade union, works council, joint committee); % covered by H&S committees
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and jurisdictionally specific. Report collective bargaining coverage as % by country. Distinguish types of worker representation (certified trade unions, works councils, European Works Council). Disclose whether non-employees are covered. Reference applicable national labour law frameworks.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when own workforce is material. Phased-in for ≤750 employees Year 1.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Diversity metrics (gender diversity in governance and workforce)
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 405-1 (Diversity of governance bodies and employees — gender, age, minority groups). BRSR Principle 3 (gender diversity by category). GRI 405-1 is the direct crossmap — covers gender and age diversity by governance level. GRI 405-1 reporters satisfy S1-9 core metrics with the addition of the three-tier governance breakdown required by ESRS.
De-duplication Notes: GRI 405-1 is structurally equivalent. Key ESRS addition: explicit board/senior management/total workforce three-tier breakdown. EU Gender Balance on Boards Directive (applicable to large listed companies) introduces a formal target that can be referenced in this disclosure.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit S1-9 in Year 1 [Column L, Appendix C of ESRS 1]
Schema / Unit: % — gender diversity by governance level (board, senior management, total workforce), age group distribution (under 30, 30–50, over 50), disability disclosure rate where available
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and structured by category. Report percentages by governance level and age band. Reference any diversity targets set under EU Gender Balance on Boards Directive where applicable. State data collection methodology for disability metrics (voluntary self-identification rate). Avoid binary-only gender reporting where systems allow three-category capture.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when own workforce is assessed as material. Disclose diversity metrics for gender and age across governance levels. Phased-in for ≤750 employees in Year 1.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Adequate wages
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S1-10 (adequate wages) is not TNFD-native. TNFD can only be used as contextual risk lens where nature-related supply chains and remote operations influence wage adequacy risk. Keep ESRS/ILO framing primary; TNFD adds no new wage metric requirements.
De-duplication Notes: No TNFD-specific wage dataset required. Collect once via HR compensation systems; optionally segment by nature-linked operations if material for risk management.
Phased-in Details: Column L: significant phased-in provisions; deferral available per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: % of employees earning below adequate wage benchmark; comparison of lowest wage to applicable living wage benchmarks by country; whether a living wage commitment has been adopted and timeline
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and jurisdictionally specific. Compare lowest wages to national living wage benchmarks (Anker methodology or equivalent) and statutory minimum wage by country. State % of employees below adequate wage threshold. Disclose whether a living wage commitment has been made and the timeline for achieving it.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Own Workforce topic is material.
Calculation Standard: EU Adequate Minimum Wage Directive (2022/2041); national minimum wage benchmarks per operating country
Disaggregation Dimensions: By country / by employee category / by gender
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: context-only; ESRS remains primary disclosure format.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: % of employees; EUR or local currency ratio
GRI: % — GRI 202-1 (ratios of standard entry level wage by gender compared to local minimum wage)

DP Name: Own Workforce — Social protection
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S1-11 (social protection) is not TNFD-native. TNFD only intersects indirectly where nature-related field operations rely on contractors/seasonal labour and require robust protections. Treat as standard HR disclosure; reference TNFD only if nature programme changes workforce composition materially.
De-duplication Notes: No TNFD-specific dataset required; collect via HR/payroll systems. Use TNFD only as contextual note where nature-related operating model changes workforce risk profile.
Phased-in Details: Column L: phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: % of employees covered by social protection by category (sickness, unemployment, work injury, parental leave, old-age/pension); statutory vs. company-provided; by country
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and jurisdictionally precise. Report coverage by social protection category. Distinguish statutory coverage from voluntary company-provided coverage (private health, occupational pension, income protection). Report by country for multinationals. State gaps in coverage by category or geography.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Own Workforce topic is material.
Calculation Standard: ILO Social Protection Floor Recommendation No. 202
Disaggregation Dimensions: By social protection type (health / unemployment / disability / pension / parental leave) / by country / by employment category
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: context-only; ESRS remains primary disclosure format.
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: % of employees
GRI: % — GRI 401-2 (benefits provided to full-time employees not provided to temporary or part-time employees)

DP Name: Own Workforce — Persons with disabilities
Cross-Framework Bridge: No direct equivalent in GRI, CDP, TCFD, or IFRS S1/S2. GRI 405-1 mentions 'other indicators of diversity' as optional but does not specifically require disability disclosure. ESRS S1-12 is ESRS-specific. The UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) and applicable national disability legislation provide the reference framework.
De-duplication Notes: ESRS-specific — no direct crossmap with any major ESG framework. This is a gap disclosure for companies reporting GRI 405-1. S1-12 requires dedicated data collection infrastructure not covered by any existing voluntary framework standard.
Phased-in Details: Column L: phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: % and headcount of employees with disclosed disabilities; by country where legally permissible; accommodation measures in place; methodology and data collection constraints documented
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative with sensitivity to data collection constraints. Acknowledge jurisdiction-specific limitations (GDPR, local data protection). Describe reasonable accommodation measures. Note voluntary self-identification approach where used. State whether data is based on self-declaration or HR system records.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when own workforce is material. Phased-in per Appendix C.
Calculation Standard: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities definitions
Disaggregation Dimensions: By region / by employee category

DP Name: Own Workforce — Training and skills development metrics
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 404-1 (Average hours of training per year per employee by gender and employee category). GRI 404-3 (Percentage of employees receiving regular performance and career development reviews). GRI 404-1 and 404-3 directly satisfy the core metrics in S1-13. Collect once to GRI 404 standard; reformat for ESRS.
De-duplication Notes: GRI 404-1 and 404-3 are functionally equivalent to S1-13 core metrics. Single data collection satisfies both. Key ESRS addition: reskilling/skills transition metric not required by GRI 404 standard.
Phased-in Details: Year 1 exemption for ≤750 employees; Column L additional phased-in sub-elements
Schema / Unit: Average training hours per employee per year by gender and employee category; % employees in regular performance and career development reviews; % accessing reskilling/upskilling programmes
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and category-specific. Report training hours by gender and employee category. Distinguish formal training from on-the-job learning. Report performance review participation %. Include skills transition data (reskilling/upskilling programme coverage). Reference any digital or green skills transition programmes.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when own workforce is material. Phased-in for ≤750 employees Year 1.
Calculation Standard: Training hours per FTE as per ILO definitions
Disaggregation Dimensions: By employee category / by gender / by training type (technical / leadership / compliance / sustainability)
Framework Schema Variants: GRI: GRI 404-1 + GRI 404-3 — ESRS combines these into one DP; GRI treats as separate disclosures; GRI 404-1 = average hours; GRI 404-3 = % receiving regular performance and career development reviews
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: Hours per employee; %
GRI: Hours — GRI 404-1 (average hours of training per year per employee) by gender and employee category

DP Name: Own Workforce — Health and safety metrics
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 403-9 (Work-related injuries — rates, fatalities, lost day rate). GRI 403-10 (Work-related ill health — cases of recordable ill health). GRI 403-9 and 403-10 are near-identical to ESRS S1-14 — same ILO-based metrics, same structure. One of the strongest 1:1 crossmaps in S1.
De-duplication Notes: GRI 403-9/10 and ESRS S1-14 are functionally equivalent. Single data collection covers both entirely. Ensure non-employee worker disaggregation is captured — required by both GRI 403 and ESRS S1-14.
Phased-in Details: Year 1 exemption for ≤750 employees; Column L additional phased-in sub-elements
Schema / Unit: Lost Time Injury Rate (LTIR), Recordable Injury Rate, Lost Days Rate, work-related fatalities, occupational disease rate; disaggregated by employees and non-employee workers
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and statistically rigorous. Report using standard ILO/OSHA definitions. Disaggregate by employee and non-employee workers. State rate base (per 1 million hours worked — specify). Include fatalities separately. Report occupational disease incidence where tracked. State boundary (management control vs. equity share).
Trigger Condition: Triggered when own workforce is material. Phased-in for ≤750 employees Year 1.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Work-life balance metrics
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 401-3 (Parental leave — % entitled, return-to-work rate, retention rate, by gender). GRI 401-3 parental leave data directly satisfies the parental leave component of S1-15. ESRS S1-15 adds flexible/remote working arrangement data not covered by GRI 401-3.
De-duplication Notes: GRI 401-3 is the primary crossmap for the parental leave element. Flexible working metrics are ESRS-specific — no direct GRI equivalent. Collect GRI 401-3 data plus additional flexible/remote working data for full S1-15 coverage.
Phased-in Details: Year 1 exemption for ≤750 employees; Column L additional phased-in sub-elements
Schema / Unit: % employees entitled to parental leave; % taking parental leave; return-to-work rate after parental leave — by gender; flexible/remote working availability and uptake rates
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and gender-disaggregated. Report parental leave entitlement, take-up rate, and return-to-work rate by gender. Include flexible and remote working availability and uptake rates. Reference national parental leave legislation baseline. Note any enhanced company provisions above statutory minimum.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when own workforce is material. Phased-in for ≤750 employees Year 1.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Remuneration metrics (pay gap and total remuneration)
Cross-Framework Bridge: GRI 2-21 (Annual total compensation ratio — CEO pay ratio). GRI 405-2 (Ratio of basic salary and remuneration of women to men — pay gap). GRI 2-21 and 405-2 directly map to S1-16. Pay gap (GRI 405-2) and CEO pay ratio (GRI 2-21) together satisfy the core S1-16 requirements. EU Pay Transparency Directive (effective 2026) will standardize pay gap methodology across EU.
De-duplication Notes: GRI 2-21 (CEO pay ratio) and GRI 405-2 (gender pay gap) together constitute S1-16. Most companies not yet disclosing these will need to build HR analytics capability. EU Pay Transparency Directive will mandate pay gap reporting independently — align S1-16 methodology with Directive requirements.
Phased-in Details: Column L: pay gap and pay ratio sub-elements subject to phased-in per Appendix C of ESRS 1
Schema / Unit: % — gender pay gap (mean and median), CEO pay ratio (CEO total remuneration vs. median employee), total remuneration components by category where applicable
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and methodology-explicit. Report gender pay gap as both mean and median. State calculation methodology (equal pay for equal work vs. overall gender pay gap). Reference EU Pay Transparency Directive alignment. CEO pay ratio must state the denominator (median total compensation of all employees, excluding CEO). Flag any restatements from prior year.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when own workforce is assessed as material. Phased-in — gender pay gap may be omitted in early years where HR data systems do not support it. CEO pay ratio increasingly required. ≤750 employees undertakings may omit in Year 1.

DP Name: Own Workforce — Incidents, complaints and severe human rights impacts concerning own workforce
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S1-17 (incidents/complaints/severe human rights impacts for own workforce) is not TNFD-native. TNFD can be used only to contextualise incident risk where nature-related field operations increase H&S or rights risks (remote sites, contractor-heavy work). Keep ESRS as the primary incident disclosure; TNFD adds optional segmentation by nature-related operations for management learning.
De-duplication Notes: No TNFD-specific incident dataset required. Optionally tag incidents linked to nature-related field operations to support integrated risk learning across TNFD and ESRS governance.
Phased-in Details: Year 1 exemption for ≤750 employees; Column L additional phased-in sub-elements
Schema / Unit: Number of work-related incidents and complaints by type (discrimination, harassment, H&S, wage theft, forced labour); number received/investigated/resolved; legal actions filed; severe human rights violations identified
Tonality Requirement: Factual and legally precise. Report confirmed incidents only. State number received, investigated, resolved, and outstanding. Distinguish H&S incidents (also in S1-14) from human rights violations specifically. Reference legal proceedings with neutral language. Avoid admissions of liability.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when incidents exist and Own Workforce topic is material.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: optional context tagging; ESRS requires incident metrics and remediation narrative.

DP Name: Value Chain Workers — Policies related to value chain workers
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S2-1 (policies for value chain workers) can incorporate TNFD due diligence discipline where nature-related supply chain hotspots create labour risk (e.g., high-risk commodities from biodiversity-sensitive areas, water-stressed regions). Use TNFD hotspot mapping to prioritise supplier labour policies, responsible sourcing policies, and audit scope; disclose in ESRS worker-rights policy framing.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse one responsible sourcing policy and supplier code of conduct that covers both nature and labour risks; TNFD provides prioritisation (where to focus), ESRS S2-1 provides the worker-rights disclosure framing.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit all S2 DPs for first 2 years [Appendix C of ESRS 1, Column K]
Schema / Unit: Policy descriptions covering due diligence on labour rights in supply chain, supplier codes of conduct, and remediation commitments
Tonality Requirement: Policy language aligned with UN Guiding Principles (UNGP) and OECD Guidelines. Reference the company's supply chain due diligence policy and supplier code of conduct. State coverage (tier 1 vs. multi-tier) and enforcement mechanisms. Reference EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) alignment where applicable.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Value Chain Workers topic is material and policies exist; disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Nature hotspot framing; ESRS: labour-rights policy disclosure for value chain workers.

DP Name: Value Chain Workers — Processes for engaging with value chain workers about impacts
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S2-2 (engagement with value chain workers) can reuse TNFD LEAP engagement guidance where nature-related value chain risks (e.g., deforestation-linked commodities, water-stressed sourcing regions) create worker impacts and require consultation. Use TNFD stakeholder engagement methods as a template; ESRS requires worker-rights framing and value chain labour context.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD engagement covered suppliers/communities, adapt the engagement evidence pack to include worker representatives and labour-rights channels; avoid duplicating engagement programmes.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — engagement approaches (direct vs. proxies); methodologies for capturing worker perspectives; consultation with unions/NGOs/ombudspersons; how input influences supply chain management decisions
Tonality Requirement: Process-oriented and rights-aligned. Describe how value chain workers' views are sought — directly (where accessible) or via legitimate proxies (NGOs, trade union federations, ombudspersons). Acknowledge barriers to direct engagement. Reference UNGP stakeholder engagement criteria. State whether engagement is verified by independent third parties.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Value Chain Workers topic is material.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Engagement focuses on IPLCs/affected stakeholders; ESRS S2-2 requires value chain worker engagement specifics (channels, frequency, topics, integration into decisions).

DP Name: Value Chain Workers — Processes to remediate negative impacts and channels to raise concerns
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S2-3 (remediation/channels for value chain workers) can reuse TNFD/UNGP-aligned due diligence approach by documenting worker grievance mechanisms accessible to supplier workers, escalation paths, and remediation outcomes—especially in nature-linked supply chains where community and labour impacts co-occur. TNFD provides process discipline; ESRS requires worker-specific channel disclosure.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse the same grievance mechanism architecture used for TNFD stakeholder engagement, but add worker-specific accessibility (language, anonymity, retaliation protection) for value chain workers.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — grievance mechanism accessibility for value chain workers; supplier corrective action plan process; remediation processes; number of supply chain grievances received and resolved where disclosed
Tonality Requirement: Process-oriented and accessibility-focused. Describe grievance mechanisms accessible to workers employed by suppliers — not just company's own mechanism. Reference UNGP effectiveness criteria. State whether workers can raise concerns without risk of reprisal. Include third-party grievance hotline where used.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Value Chain Workers topic is material and impacts exist; phased-in may apply.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: engagement/due diligence; ESRS requires explicit worker grievance channels and remediation disclosure.

DP Name: Value Chain Workers — Actions related to material impacts on value chain workers
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S2-4 (actions) can use TNFD LEAP outputs to prioritise supply chain locations where both nature impacts and labour risks are high (e.g., deforestation-linked sourcing regions). Use a unified supplier improvement plan (audits, corrective action plans, capacity building, living wage programmes) and disclose actions/resources in ESRS format.
De-duplication Notes: Maintain one supplier action register; TNFD provides hotspot prioritisation, ESRS provides labour impact action disclosure structure.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit S2 DPs for first 2 years [Appendix C of ESRS 1]
Schema / Unit: Narrative describing remediation actions, supplier capacity-building programmes, and audit outcomes for material labour rights impacts in the value chain
Tonality Requirement: Action-oriented and impact-specific. Describe concrete remediation steps taken for identified material impacts. Reference supplier audit results, corrective action plan completion rates, and capacity-building initiatives. Distinguish between actions taken by the undertaking vs. by suppliers. Reference UNGP remedy framework if applicable.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Value Chain Workers topic is material and actions exist.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: actions framed as nature-risk response in value chain; ESRS requires value chain worker impact remediation actions.

DP Name: Value Chain Workers — Targets related to managing material negative impacts on value chain workers
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S2-5 (targets) can reuse TNFD metrics/targets discipline for supplier programme KPIs where nature-linked value chains are in scope (e.g., % high-risk suppliers covered by audits, % corrective actions closed, grievance resolution time). TNFD supplies prioritisation and governance for target-setting; ESRS requires baseline, timeline, and progress disclosure.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse the same target register format as TNFD (baseline, target year, progress) and ensure ESRS-required disclosures are explicit for worker outcomes and supplier coverage.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Supply chain labour targets — metric (% suppliers audited, % corrective action closure rate, living wage coverage in tier 1), base year, target year, external standard commitment (SA8000, amfori BSCI, Sedex)
Tonality Requirement: Precise and time-bound. State targets with specific metrics, base year, and target year. Include accountability. Reference supply chain standards committed to. Pair each target with current-year progress metric. State whether targets are linked to procurement decisions.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Value Chain Workers topic is material and targets exist; disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: targets may be framed as programme KPIs; ESRS requires worker-impact target framing and disclosure.

DP Name: Affected Communities — Policies related to affected communities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S3-1 (policies for affected communities) can reuse TNFD LEAP guidance on meaningful engagement and due diligence (UNGP-aligned), especially where nature-related impacts (land use change, water access/quality impacts, biodiversity offsets) affect communities and IPLCs. Use TNFD governance and engagement artifacts (policy register, FPIC commitments, benefit-sharing policies) and render into ESRS MDR-P structure for affected communities.
