De-duplication Notes: If TNFD already has policies on IPLC engagement/FPIC, land access, resettlement avoidance, and benefit sharing for nature-related projects, reuse them as the policy source-of-truth for S3-1; add ESRS-required structure and gap disclosure where no policy exists for a material impact.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit all S3 DPs for first 2 years [Appendix C of ESRS 1, Column K]
Schema / Unit: Policy descriptions covering community engagement, free prior and informed consent (FPIC), land rights, and human rights due diligence for affected communities
Tonality Requirement: Policy language grounded in UNGP and IFC Performance Standards. Reference FPIC commitments for indigenous peoples where applicable. Name community engagement and grievance mechanism policies. State scope (which operations/geographies) and governance ownership. Reference any social impact assessment (SIA) commitments.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Affected Communities topic is material and policies exist; disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Policies may be embedded in engagement/due diligence guidance; ESRS requires explicit policy disclosure for affected communities with MDR-P-style elements (scope, commitments, implementation, monitoring).

DP Name: Affected Communities — Processes for engaging with affected communities about impacts
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S3-2 (engagement with affected communities) is strongly supported by TNFD guidance on engagement with Indigenous Peoples, Local Communities (IPLCs) and affected stakeholders during LEAP. Reuse TNFD engagement plans, FPIC processes where applicable, grievance inputs, and documentation of how community views informed impact/risk assessment and response planning. Key delta: ESRS requires social-topic framing and material impact focus; TNFD provides a nature-linked engagement methodology and evidence pack.
De-duplication Notes: If LEAP engagement work exists, reuse it as the core evidence for S3-2 for nature-linked affected communities; broaden only where additional social impacts exist beyond nature interfaces.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — community engagement methods (consultations, ESIAs, liaison offices, participatory mapping); FPIC processes for indigenous communities; frequency and accessibility of engagement
Tonality Requirement: Place-specific and rights-aligned. Describe community engagement methods at site or regional level. For indigenous and local communities, describe FPIC processes explicitly referencing UNDRIP. Identify community engagement officers/mechanisms. State how engagement findings are incorporated into site-level decisions.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Affected Communities topic is material; engagement processes are expected where impacts exist.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Engagement is embedded in LEAP and due diligence; ESRS S3-2 requires structured disclosure of engagement methods, stakeholder groups, and how views influenced decisions.

DP Name: Affected Communities — Processes to remediate negative impacts and channels to raise concerns
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S3-3 (remediation and channels for raising concerns) can reuse TNFD engagement and due diligence guidance (linked to UNGP) by documenting grievance mechanisms, remediation pathways, escalation, and outcomes for communities affected by nature-related issues (land use change, water impacts, biodiversity impacts). TNFD supports the evidence approach; ESRS requires structured social remediation disclosure.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse the same grievance mechanism and remediation workflow documentation used for TNFD/UNGP-aligned due diligence as the basis for S3-3; ensure community-specific accessibility is documented.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — community grievance mechanism accessibility (local language, in-person, digital); remediation processes for community-level harms; number and type of community grievances received and resolved
Tonality Requirement: Process-oriented and accessibility-focused. Describe community grievance mechanism accessibility in local language, physical format, and for non-literate community members. Reference UNGP effectiveness criteria. State number of community grievances received and resolved. Include third-party mechanism (ombudsman, independent mediator) where used.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Affected Communities topic is material and impacts exist; disclose channels regardless where relevant.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Focus on meaningful engagement and due diligence; ESRS requires explicit remediation channels, process, and accessibility details.

DP Name: Affected Communities — Actions related to material impacts on affected communities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S3-4 (actions) can be supported by TNFD Prepare-stage action registers where actions address community impacts linked to nature (e.g., water stewardship with local users, land restoration with community co-management, biodiversity offsets with benefit sharing). Use TNFD LEAP outputs to prioritise locations and affected groups; report actions, resources, and effectiveness tracking in ESRS structure.
De-duplication Notes: If TNFD action register includes community engagement and benefit-sharing actions, reuse it for S3-4 and add ESRS-specific detail on remediation of social impacts and resource allocation.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit all S3 DPs for first 2 years [Appendix C of ESRS 1]
Schema / Unit: Narrative of community investment, remediation actions, grievance resolution outcomes, and shared value initiatives for materially impacted communities
Tonality Requirement: Impact-specific and place-based. Describe actions per community or region where material impacts exist. Reference grievance mechanism outcomes (complaints received, resolved, pending). Include both short-term remediation and longer-term shared value/community development actions. Reference social impact assessment outcomes where conducted.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Affected Communities topic is material and actions exist.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Actions may be framed as nature response plans; ESRS requires explicit affected-community action disclosure (social impact management).

DP Name: Affected Communities — Targets related to managing material negative impacts on affected communities
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S3-5 (targets) can reuse TNFD Metrics & Targets discipline where targets relate to community outcomes tied to nature-related actions (e.g., % sites with FPIC process, grievance resolution time, community benefit-sharing commitments linked to biodiversity projects). TNFD provides the governance/methodology for target setting; ESRS requires social-topic target disclosure with baseline, timeline, and progress.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse TNFD target register structure for community-related targets where nature-linked; ensure ESRS-required baseline and progress reporting is present.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Community impact targets — metric (# FPIC processes completed, community investment as % revenue, grievance resolution rate %), base year, target year, site-level applicability
Tonality Requirement: Precise and site-specific. State targets with specific metrics. Include FPIC process completion targets for indigenous community operations. Reference community investment methodology. Pair with current-year progress.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Affected Communities topic is material and targets exist; disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Targets may be captured under governance/engagement; ESRS requires MDR-T-like structure for social targets (baseline, milestones, progress, gap disclosure).

DP Name: Affected Communities — Community investment / CSR spend and outcomes (entity-specific)
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S3 CSR-1 (community investment spend/outcomes) is entity-specific, but can be aligned with TNFD Prepare actions where community investment is part of nature-related mitigation/benefit-sharing (e.g., watershed projects, restoration co-benefits, IPLC benefit-sharing). Use TNFD LEAP priority locations to justify where community investment is focused and how outcomes are measured.
De-duplication Notes: Do not create separate TNFD ‘CSR spend’ reporting. If community investment is a TNFD response action (benefit sharing, restoration partnership), reference the same programme register for CSR-1 outcomes tracking.
Schema / Unit: ₹ — spend totals and allocation; count — beneficiaries; mixed — outcome KPIs
Standard Reference: Entity-specific S3 support datapoint (use when affected communities topic is material)
Trigger Condition: Entity-specific: disclose if the undertaking uses community investment/CSR as a response to material impacts on affected communities.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: investment framed as response/benefit-sharing in priority landscapes; ESRS CSR-1 requires spend + outcomes reporting (entity-specific definition).
Framework Unit Variants:
ESRS: ₹, counts; program-specific outcome metrics (varies)
GRI: currency + program breakdown; sometimes % of profit; narrative definitions
BRSR: ₹ and prescribed table formats

DP Name: Consumers & End-users — Policies related to consumers and end-users
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S4-1 (policies for consumers/end-users) is not TNFD-native, but TNFD can contribute where nature-related product impacts or nature-related claims create consumer harm risk (e.g., toxicity, water impacts, misleading ‘nature-positive’ marketing). Use TNFD risk/opportunity register to identify these product impact pathways and ensure consumer protection policies include nature-related claim integrity and environmental safety commitments.
De-duplication Notes: No TNFD-specific consumer policy dataset needed. Reference TNFD only where nature-related impact pathways or claims are material; otherwise treat S4-1 as standard consumer policy disclosure.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit all S4 DPs for first 2 years [Appendix C of ESRS 1, Column K]
Schema / Unit: Policy descriptions covering product safety, responsible marketing, data privacy, consumer grievance mechanisms, and vulnerable consumer protection
Tonality Requirement: Policy language aligned with EU consumer protection regulation (GDPR, Consumer Rights Directive, Product Safety Regulation). Name specific policies (product safety policy, responsible marketing policy, data privacy policy). State scope, governance ownership, and any relevant certifications (ISO 27001, CE marking processes).
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Consumers & End-users topic is material and policies exist; disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: adds nature-claims integrity lens; ESRS requires consumer/end-user policy disclosure.

DP Name: Consumers & End-users — Processes for engaging with consumers and end-users about impacts
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S4-2 (engagement with consumers/end-users) can reuse TNFD stakeholder engagement discipline only indirectly: where nature-related product impacts or claims are material, consumer research and feedback loops (complaints analysis, surveys, product safety feedback) should be used as ‘stakeholder input’ into LEAP Prepare decisions. TNFD provides the engagement logic; ESRS requires consumer-specific engagement disclosure.
De-duplication Notes: No TNFD-specific dataset required. Reuse product safety/customer support engagement metrics; reference TNFD only when consumer feedback directly influenced nature-related risk/opportunity management.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — consumer engagement and feedback methods (surveys, product testing panels, complaint channels, social listening, user research with persons with disabilities); how feedback informs product/service decisions
Tonality Requirement: Consumer-centric and process-oriented. Describe formal and informal consumer engagement channels. Reference post-purchase feedback, product safety consultation, and accessibility testing. State how consumer feedback is escalated to product development and governance decisions.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Consumers & End-users topic is material.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: engagement discipline; ESRS requires consumer engagement process disclosure.

DP Name: Consumers & End-users — Processes to remediate negative impacts and channels to raise concerns
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S4-3 (remediation and channels) can reuse TNFD due diligence approach for stakeholder grievance and remediation where consumer/end-user impacts arise from nature-related product externalities (e.g., water quality impacts, product toxicity, nature-related claims). TNFD provides process discipline; ESRS requires consumer/end-user specific accessibility and response measures.
De-duplication Notes: Use one grievance/remediation architecture across stakeholder types. TNFD contributes UNGP-aligned design principles; ESRS S4-3 requires consumer-specific channels and metrics.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Narrative — consumer complaint and grievance mechanism design; product recall processes; data breach notification; redress mechanisms; complaints received, investigated, and resolved
Tonality Requirement: Process-oriented and regulatory-aligned. Describe consumer complaint mechanism (accessibility, response time, resolution process). Reference EU Consumer Rights Directive and ADR requirements. State average resolution time. Include product recall escalation and data breach notification mechanism.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Consumers & End-users topic is material.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: Due diligence engagement; ESRS requires explicit consumer/end-user channels and remediation outcomes disclosure.

DP Name: Consumers & End-users — Actions related to material impacts on consumers and end-users
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S4-4 (actions) can intersect with TNFD where actions address consumer/end-user impacts linked to nature (e.g., product reformulation to reduce toxicity, packaging redesign to reduce marine litter, improved product stewardship in sensitive markets). Use TNFD LEAP outputs to prioritise where product externalities create nature and consumer impacts; disclose action plans and resources in ESRS format.
De-duplication Notes: Maintain one product stewardship action register. TNFD provides prioritised nature-impact hotspots; ESRS provides consumer impact action disclosure structure.
Phased-in Details: Undertakings ≤750 employees may omit all S4 DPs for first 2 years [Appendix C of ESRS 1]
Schema / Unit: Narrative of product safety actions, recall events, misleading marketing remediation, data breach responses, and grievance resolution outcomes for consumers
Tonality Requirement: Action-specific and consumer-rights grounded. Describe concrete actions taken for each identified material impact category (safety, privacy, marketing). Reference product recall events and corrective actions. Include consumer complaint volume and resolution rate. Reference any regulatory enforcement actions and company response. Use neutral, factual language — avoid minimizing tone.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Consumers & End-users topic is material and actions exist.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: actions framed as nature-risk response; ESRS requires consumer impact remediation actions.

DP Name: Consumers & End-users — Targets related to managing material negative impacts on consumers and end-users
Cross-Framework Bridge: TNFD alignment: ESRS S4-5 (targets) can reuse TNFD metrics/targets discipline where targets relate to consumer outcomes linked to nature-related product impacts (e.g., reduction in hazardous substances, complaint resolution SLAs for environmental harm claims, packaging recovery targets impacting marine litter). TNFD provides prioritisation and governance; ESRS requires baseline, timeline, and progress disclosure.
De-duplication Notes: Reuse TNFD target register structure where nature-linked; ensure ESRS-required progress reporting is explicit for consumer outcomes.
Phased-in Details: Years 1–2 for ≤750 employees
Schema / Unit: Consumer impact targets — metric (complaint resolution rate %, product safety improvement rate %, data breach reduction, accessibility score improvement), base year, target year, governance accountability
Tonality Requirement: Precise and consumer-rights-aligned. State targets with specific metrics. Include product safety, complaint resolution, and data privacy improvement targets. Reference EU product liability and consumer rights framework alignment where applicable.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Consumers & End-users topic is material and targets exist; disclose absence where required.
Framework Schema Variants: TNFD: targets may be framed as product impact KPIs; ESRS requires consumer-impact target framing and disclosure.

DP Name: GRI 2-7 — Employees
Cross-Framework Bridge: ESRS S1-6 (Characteristics of the undertaking's employees) — near-identical in metric definition and breakdown structure. GRI 2-7 data collection directly satisfies ESRS S1-6. Collect once; reformat heading labels per framework output.
De-duplication Notes: Reverse crossmap to ESRS-S1-6. GRI 2-7 and ESRS S1-6 are functionally equivalent. Headcount data collected for GRI 2-7 satisfies S1-6 with minimal reformatting.
Schema / Unit: Headcount — total employees by gender, employment type (permanent/temporary), full-time/part-time, region; year-end and average figures
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and demographically precise. Report headcount (not FTE unless additionally requested). Gender split mandatory. Include regional disaggregation for multinationals. State whether data covers all subsidiaries. Report both year-end and average headcount.
Trigger Condition: Required for all GRI reporters under GRI 2 (Universal Standards). Not contingent on materiality — foundational organisational data.

DP Name: GRI 205-3 — Confirmed incidents of corruption and actions taken
Cross-Framework Bridge: ESRS G1-4 (Confirmed incidents of corruption or bribery) — near-identical in metric definition, reporting structure, and outcome categorisation. GRI 205-3 data directly satisfies ESRS G1-4. Collect once; report to both with identical narrative framing.
De-duplication Notes: Strongest 1:1 reverse crossmap in G1. GRI 205-3 and ESRS G1-4 are functionally equivalent. Anti-corruption incident register collected for GRI 205-3 satisfies G1-4 with no additional data collection.
Schema / Unit: Number of confirmed corruption incidents; by type; actions taken (dismissal, prosecution, contract termination); legal cases filed
Tonality Requirement: Factual and legally neutral. Report confirmed incidents only (not allegations). State actions taken per incident. Distinguish employee vs. third-party incidents. Use neutral legal language — avoid admissions of liability.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when anti-corruption is material under GRI 3-3. Required for all companies disclosing GRI 205.

DP Name: GRI 303-3 — Water withdrawal
Cross-Framework Bridge: ESRS E3-4 (Water consumption — withdrawal component). CDP Water C8 (water withdrawal). GRI 303-3 withdrawal data is the primary input for ESRS E3-4 and CDP C8. Collect once; ESRS adds the consumption (withdrawal minus discharge) calculation on top.
De-duplication Notes: Reverse crossmap to ESRS-E3-4. GRI 303-3 water withdrawal data is the upstream input that feeds ESRS E3-4 withdrawal and CDP Water C8. Water-stressed area disaggregation satisfies ESRS and improves CDP scoring simultaneously.
Schema / Unit: Megalitres — total water withdrawal by source (surface water, groundwater, seawater, produced water, third-party water); water-stressed area disaggregation
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and source-specific. Report by water source. Disaggregate for water-stressed areas using a recognised stress tool (WRI Aqueduct, etc.). State methodology. Include third-party/municipal water separately.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when water is material under GRI 3-3. Core quantitative water metric for any GRI-aligned reporter in water-intensive sectors.

DP Name: GRI 305-1 — Direct (Scope 1) GHG emissions
Cross-Framework Bridge: ESRS E1-6 (Scope 1 GHG emissions) — near-identical metric. TCFD Metrics & Targets (Scope 1). IFRS S2 para. 29 (Scope 1). CDP C6.1. GRI 305-1 data satisfies all four frameworks' Scope 1 requirement. Collect once to GHG Protocol standard; reformat boundary and unit presentation per framework.
De-duplication Notes: GRI 305-1 is the reverse-crossmap anchor for ESRS-E1-6. Single Scope 1 data collection satisfies GRI 305-1, ESRS E1-6, TCFD, IFRS S2, and CDP C6. No duplication needed.
Schema / Unit: tCO2e — gross direct Scope 1 GHG emissions; by gas (CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6, NF3); consolidation approach; base year
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and methodologically explicit. State consolidation approach (operational control, financial control, equity share). Report by gas where feasible. Reference GHG Protocol Corporate Standard. Include biogenic CO2 separately if applicable.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when climate/GHG emissions is identified as a material topic under GRI 3-3. Standard GHG data collection requirement for any GRI-aligned reporter.

DP Name: GRI 305-2 — Energy indirect (Scope 2) GHG emissions
Cross-Framework Bridge: ESRS E1-6 (Scope 2 GHG emissions). TCFD Metrics & Targets. IFRS S2 para. 29. CDP C6.3. GRI 305-2 dual-reporting (location + market) satisfies all frameworks. ESRS E1-6 requires both methods; GRI 305-2 is directly equivalent.
De-duplication Notes: Reverse crossmap to ESRS-E1-6. Scope 2 collected once (both methods) covers GRI 305-2, ESRS E1-6, TCFD, IFRS S2, and CDP C6. Key: ensure market-based figure uses correct contractual instrument data.
Schema / Unit: tCO2e — location-based AND market-based Scope 2 emissions; consolidation approach; emission factors used
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative. Report both location-based and market-based figures (dual reporting). State emission factors used per grid/supplier. Reference GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance. Include contractual instruments (RECs, PPAs) in market-based calculation.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when climate/GHG emissions is material. GRI 305-2 requires both location-based and market-based Scope 2 figures.

DP Name: GRI 305-3 — Other indirect (Scope 3) GHG emissions
Cross-Framework Bridge: ESRS E1-6 (Scope 3 GHG emissions — all categories). TCFD Metrics & Targets (Scope 3 where relevant). IFRS S2 para. 29 (Scope 3). CDP C6.5/C6.10. GRI 305-3 by-category structure directly maps to ESRS E1-6 Scope 3 requirements. Collect once; both frameworks use GHG Protocol category structure.
De-duplication Notes: Reverse crossmap to ESRS-E1-6 Scope 3 component. GRI 305-3 and ESRS E1-6 Scope 3 are functionally identical — same GHG Protocol categories, same estimation logic. One Scope 3 inventory covers all.
Schema / Unit: tCO2e — Scope 3 emissions by category (GHG Protocol categories 1–15); data quality and estimation methodology per category
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative with transparency on estimation. Report by GHG Protocol Scope 3 category. State data quality (measured, calculated, estimated) per category. Identify significant categories. Reference SBTI sectoral pathways where applicable.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when Scope 3/value chain emissions is material. GRI 305-3 requires disclosure of all significant Scope 3 categories with methodology.

DP Name: GRI 306-3 — Waste generated
Cross-Framework Bridge: ESRS E5-5 (Resource outflows including waste — total waste generated component). GRI 306-3 is the upstream data input for the waste generation element of ESRS E5-5. GRI 306-4 (diverted from disposal) and 306-5 (directed to disposal) cover the disposal route breakdown also required by E5-5.
De-duplication Notes: Reverse crossmap to ESRS-E5-5. GRI 306-3/4/5 series and ESRS E5-5 are functionally equivalent. Waste data collected for GRI 306 series directly satisfies E5-5 with the same hazardous/non-hazardous and disposal method structure.
Schema / Unit: Tonnes — total waste generated by hazardous/non-hazardous split and composition (by type where feasible); per unit output intensity optional
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative. Report total waste by hazardous/non-hazardous classification. Include composition breakdown where available (e.g. plastic, organic, electronic). Reference Basel Convention for hazardous waste definition. State whether data covers all operations or excludes any.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when waste is material under GRI 3-3. Core waste generation metric for any GRI-aligned reporter.

DP Name: GRI 405-1 — Diversity of governance bodies and employees
Cross-Framework Bridge: ESRS S1-9 (Diversity metrics — gender, age group). GRI 405-1 data collection is near-identical to ESRS S1-9. Collect once to GRI 405-1 standard; the board-level diversity data also feeds ESRS 2 GOV-1 governance composition element.
De-duplication Notes: Reverse crossmap to ESRS-S1-9. GRI 405-1 and ESRS S1-9 are functionally equivalent for gender and age diversity. One data collection covers both. ESRS S1-9 may request broader dimensions in future iterations.
Schema / Unit: % and headcount — gender and age group breakdown by governance body and employee category; other diversity dimensions (minority group, etc.) where tracked
Tonality Requirement: Quantitative and demographically precise. Report by governance body level and employee category. Gender as % and headcount. Age groups: <30, 30-50, >50. Include other diversity dimensions tracked. State whether board includes independent/non-executive disaggregation.
Trigger Condition: Triggered when diversity/equal opportunity is material under GRI 3-3. Core diversity metric for GRI-aligned reporters.
